; Indiana's estimated tax: IC 6-3-4-4.1, with the penalty of IC
; 6-8.1-10-2.1(b), worked through on Schedule IT-2210, or Schedule IT-2210A
; for the annualized method. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed indianataxcalc, whose answers golden/testdata/estimated/IN.json.gz
; holds.
;
; IC 6-3-4-4.1(a) has the payments made as 26 U.S.C. § 6654 provides, so the
; tests look federal: 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, 110%
; above $150,000 of federal AGI, four quarters, nothing under $1,000. The
; charge does not. It is a flat 10% of each quarter's shortfall, so a payment
; one day late costs as much as one made months late, and making up a
; shortfall later does not reduce it. County income tax is collected with the
; state's and counts in every figure. The figures follow the department's
; forms, the 2026 Form ES-40 and the 2025 Schedules IT-2210 and IT-2210A, and
; the answer's divergences say where the Indiana Code reads otherwise. A year
; with no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the 2026 Form ES-40 prints them.
(defstruct IndianaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)))

(deffigures in-estimated-2026 IndianaEstimatedYear 2026 (from in-dor-form-es-40-2026 (threshold #usd"1000.00" :at who-must-pay) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at when-due)))

; Information Bulletin #3 and the Indiana Code give it.
(defstruct IndianaEstimatedRules (figures IndianaEstimatedYear) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (last_year_high_rate Int) (step Money) (step_separate Money) (penalty_rate Int) (file_and_pay_by Date) (period_ends (Slice Date)) (annualised_shares (Slice Int)) (zero_prior_tax Bool) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How Indiana's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= in-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Indiana wants estimated tax if you expect $1,000 or more due after withholding. The $1,000 counts state and county income tax. Its penalty is a flat 10% of each quarter's shortfall, not interest." (slice "You are clear of the penalty if you pay the smaller of two amounts. They are 90% of this year's state and county tax and 100% of last year's. Withholding, pass-through entity tax credits and estimated payments all count. Last year's figure becomes 110% if your federal AGI then was over $150,000. The limit is $75,000 if you were married filing separately. County income tax counts throughout. Indiana collects it on the same return and payment voucher." "The payments are a quarter each. They are due April 15, June 15 and September 15, 2026, and January 15, 2027. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates. You can instead show the dates it was actually taken. Filing and paying in full by January 31 replaces the January payment. For 2026 the date is February 1, 2027, because January 31 is a Sunday. If your income came unevenly, use the annualised method on Schedule IT-2210A. It can lower the early payments." "The penalty is 10% of what each quarter was short. It does not grow with time. A payment one day late costs as much as one made months later. A late payment counts toward the next quarter. An overpayment first makes up earlier shortfalls, and the rest carries forward. Making up a shortfall does not take back the 10% already charged on it. A payment made after January 15, 2027 does not count toward 2026 at all. No Indiana document says whether the federal waivers apply. They cover a casualty, disaster, retirement or disability." "Subtract withholding and pass-through credits from this year's tax. There is no penalty if what is left is under $1,000. From 2026, last year's tax can count as zero. That needs no Indiana return filed last year and no Indiana tax for it. Then nothing is required.") "Indiana charges a flat 10% of each quarter's shortfall, not interest by the day. How late you pay doesn't matter, and catching up later doesn't reduce it. County income tax counts in the $1,000 threshold and both targets. Payments after January 15 don't count." (slice "IC 6-3-4-4.1; IC 6-8.1-10-2.1(b), (d)" "Form ES-40, Estimated Tax Payment Form, 2026 (R26 / 9-25)" "Schedule IT-2210, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, and its instructions, 2025 (R27 / 9-25)" "Schedule IT-2210A, Annualized Income Schedule, 2025 (R25 / 9-25)" "Income Tax Information Bulletin #3, Payment of Indiana Estimated Tax by Individuals (March 2023)" "Indiana Department of Revenue, Legislative Synopsis 2026")))

; The 2026 rules. No 2026 IT-2210 or IT-2210A is published, so their
; arithmetic is the 2025 schedules' with the 2026 dates: line 4's 90%, line
; 7's 100% and 110% and the $150,000 and $75,000 steps, line 21's 10%, the
; installment periods, IT-2210A's percentages, and Information Bulletin #3's
; January 31. The Department's 2026 Legislative Synopsis lists no change to
; them. No Indiana holiday is listed: the four 2026 due dates and February 1,
; 2027 are weekdays. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are
; written out rather than deffigures.
(= in-estimated-rules-2026 IndianaEstimatedRules (make-struct IndianaEstimatedRules :figures in-estimated-2026 :this_year_rate 9000 :last_year_rate 10000 :last_year_high_rate 11000 :step #usd"150000.00" :step_separate #usd"75000.00" :penalty_rate 1000 :file_and_pay_by #date"2027-01-31" :period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :annualised_shares (slice 2250 4500 6750 9000) :zero_prior_tax true :explanation in-estimated-explanation))

; Kentucky's estimated tax: KRS 141.305, which adopts 26 U.S.C. § 6654 with
; four exceptions, worked through on Form 2210-K, which follows federal Form
; 2210 line for line. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed kentuckytaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/KY.json.gz holds.
;
; The shape is federal: 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, 110%
; above $150,000 of last year's Kentucky AGI, four quarters on the federal
; dates, and interest by the day. What differs is the threshold, $500 rather
; than $1,000; two income tests that decide whether payments are needed at
; all; a Kentucky rate fixed for each calendar year; and waivers only for
; reasonable cause under KRS 131.175. The figures follow the 2026 voucher
; instructions (42A740-S4) and the 2025 Form 2210-K (42A740-S1); the
; answer's divergences say where KRS 141.305 reads otherwise. A year with no
; figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as KRS 141.305 states them.
(defstruct KentuckyEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (income_test Money) (threshold Money))

(deffigures ky-estimated-2026 KentuckyEstimatedYear 2026 (from ky-legis-krs-141-305-2026 (income_test #usd"5000.00" :at subsection-1) (threshold #usd"500.00" :at subsection-2)))

; § 6654 KRS 141.305(3) adopts give it.

; How Kentucky's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ky-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Kentucky follows the federal rules closely, with a lower threshold. You need estimated payments once tax after withholding is more than $500. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall." (slice "Payments are needed if you expect over $500 of tax after withholding. Refundable credits count with withholding. You must also expect over $5,000 of income without Kentucky withholding. Expecting income high enough to need a Kentucky return counts instead. Your target is 90% of this year's Kentucky tax or 100% of last year's, if less. Withholding and payments that reach it avoid the penalty. Last year's figure needs a full-year return. It's 110% if last year's Kentucky AGI was over $150,000. That limit is $75,000 for married filing separately." "A quarter is due April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A date on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next working day. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates, whenever it was taken." "There's no penalty if this year's tax after withholding is $500 or less. There's none either if you had no Kentucky tax last year on a full-year return. As federally, each shortfall is charged for each day it stays unpaid. Charges stop at the next April 15. Each payment goes to the oldest shortfall first. Form 2210-K's annualized method can lower early payments for uneven income. Once used, it must be used for every date." "The rate is fixed for each calendar year. The department's form charges 9% for 2026. Its announced 2026 tax interest rate is 7%, and the law can be read either way. The penalty can be waived only for reasonable cause. A serious illness or a disaster that destroys your records can be one. Retirement or disability alone is not.") "Kentucky differs in its $500 threshold. Its income tests decide whether payments are needed at all. The 110% test is on Kentucky AGI, adding a combined return's incomes. The rate is fixed for the year, 9% on the form for 2026. Filing by Feb 1 excuses January only if you first had to pay after September 1. You can't elect to count withholding when withheld. Waivers need reasonable cause." (slice "KRS 141.305; KRS 131.183; KRS 131.175; 103 KAR 1:040" "Instructions for Filing Estimated Tax Vouchers 2026, 42A740-S4 (9-25), and Form 740-ES 2026, 42A740ES (10/25)" "Form 2210-K, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, 2025, 42A740-S1 (10-25), and its instructions" "KY-TAM-19-02, Requirement to Pay Estimated Tax Installments" "Department of Revenue, Tax Interest Rate Update for 01-01-26")))

; The 2026 rules. The department's documents could not be fetched for the
; catalog, and the 2026 Form 2210-K is not published, so these are the 2025
; Form 2210-K's and the 2026 voucher instructions' figures, as the Go rules
; carry them: the 90%, 100% and 110% tests and their steps, which § 6654
; supplies, the dates, the quarters, the Part III periods and percentages,
; the September 1 and January 31 of the voucher note, the April 15 stop and
; the 9% line 21 prints for 2026. A figure's source must be for its year and
; in the catalog, so these are written out rather than deffigures. The rate
; from January 1, 2027 isn't published: the rates end on December 31, 2026,
; and the penalty says so. No Kentucky holiday is listed: the four 2026 due
; dates are weekdays.

; Louisiana's estimated tax: La. R.S. 47:116 to 47:118, as Act 307 of 2026
; amends them, worked through on Form R-210R. It is written on the shared
; machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces
; the Go rules in the removed louisianataxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/LA.json.gz holds.
;
; The penalty is computed as Form R-210R computes it: a required annual
; payment, the lesser of this year's share and last year's tax, divided into
; the installments due; payments carried forward from one period to the next;
; exceptions that excuse an installment outright; and a printed daily factor
; on each shortfall for the days it was unpaid. Act 307 took effect May 22,
; 2026, after the department's latest penalty form and its estimated tax page
; were published; where those describe the old law, the figure follows the
; Act, and the divergences name the out-of-date document. A year with no
; figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as IT-540ESi (2026) prints them.
(defstruct LouisianaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (threshold_joint Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (file_and_pay_by Date))

(deffigures la-estimated-2026 LouisianaEstimatedYear 2026 (from la-ldr-it-540esi-2026 (threshold #usd"1000.00" :at who-must-pay) (threshold_joint #usd"2000.00" :at who-must-pay) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at when-due) (file_and_pay_by #date"2027-01-31" :at january-exception)))

; A tax year's rules: its figures, and what Act 307, R-210R-i and R.S.
; 47:118 give it.
(defstruct LouisianaEstimatedRules (figures LouisianaEstimatedYear) (this_year_rate Int) (later_groups (Slice Date)) (stop Date) (old_stop Date) (period_ends (Slice Date)) (daily (Slice EstRate)) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How Louisiana's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= la-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Louisiana expects estimated payments once you'll have more than $1,000 due. That's after credits and withholding, and $2,000 for a joint return. From 2026 you avoid the penalty by paying the lesser of two amounts. One is 70% of this year's tax, and the other is all of last year's." (slice "Act 307, a 2026 law, cut the required share of this year's tax from 90% to 70%. The other figure is 100% of last year's Louisiana tax. There's no higher figure for high incomes. A third test taxes last year's figures at this year's rate. It uses this year's standard deduction too. A payment date is also excused if what you paid by then reaches that tax." "Equal payments are due April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A date on a weekend or holiday is due the next business day instead. Withholding counts as paid in equal parts on the four dates. You can instead show when it was actually withheld. Filing your return with full payment by January 31 replaces the January payment. Earlier payments are still due." "The penalty is 12% a year on each shortfall, charged by the day until it's paid. From 2026 it stops on May 15 of the next year rather than April 15. A payment first makes up an earlier shortfall, then counts toward the next date. Another test taxes the income you actually earned to the end of each period. Paying 70% of that tax by the next due date also excuses that date. The department can waive the penalty if you acted in good faith. Good faith is presumed for circumstances beyond your control. It is also presumed if you declared and paid before the return was due. You apply on Form R-20128 within a year of the return's due date.") "Unlike federal, Louisiana uses 70% of this year's tax, not 90%. It has no 110% figure at higher incomes. Its threshold is $1,000 after withholding, or $2,000 on a joint return. A third test taxes last year's figures at this year's rate. Starting late means fewer, larger installments. The income-to-date test has no annualizing. The rate is a fixed 12%, and the penalty runs to May 15." (slice "La. R.S. 47:116, 47:117, 47:117.1, 47:118" "Act 307 of the 2026 Regular Session (HB 633)" "IT-540ESi (2026), Declaration of Estimated Tax for Individuals: General Information and Instructions" "R-210R-i (1/26), Underpayment of Individual Income Tax Penalty Computation, 2025" "Louisiana Department of Revenue, 2026 Legislative Summaries (June 26, 2026)")))

; The 2026 rules. Act 307's 70% and May 15 stop; R-210R-i (1/26)'s late-start
; rows, Exception 5 periods and 0.000329 daily factor, as no 2026 R-210R is
; published. The rate is fixed by R.S. 47:118(A), so one factor covers every
; day to the stop. No Louisiana holiday is listed: the four 2026 due dates are
; weekdays. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are written out
; rather than deffigures.
(= la-estimated-rules-2026 LouisianaEstimatedRules (make-struct LouisianaEstimatedRules :figures la-estimated-2026 :this_year_rate 7000 :later_groups (slice #date"2026-04-02" #date"2026-06-02" #date"2026-09-02") :stop #date"2027-05-15" :old_stop #date"2027-04-15" :period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :daily (slice (EstRate #date"2026-01-01" #date"2027-05-15" 329 "R-210R-i (1/26), Line 18: 12 percent per year, 0.0329 percent a day; La. R.S. 47:118(A)")) :explanation la-estimated-explanation))

(= la-estimated-years (Table Int LouisianaEstimatedRules) (table 2026 la-estimated-rules-2026))

; Form 1, Massachusetts Resident Income Tax Return.
;
; Massachusetts does not start from federal adjusted gross income. The return
; sorts income into classes: 5.0% income (wages, pensions, business and rental
; income) on lines 3 to 19, interest and dividends from Schedule B on line 20,
; short-term and collectibles gains at 8.5% and 12% on line 23, and long-term
; gains from Schedule D on line 24. The rules take each class from the prepared
; federal return where it carries it, and from MassachusettsInputs where it
; does not.
;
; Not modelled: Schedules B, D, X, Y and HC in detail (their results are
; inputs or come straight from the federal return), excess exemptions carried
; to Schedules B and D when line 18 exceeds line 17, No Tax Status and the
; Limited Income Credit worksheets, the optional 5.85% rate, and Schedule OJC.
;
; The rules cite the law (M.G.L. c. 62). The parts of the year's form and
; instructions they implement name them in sources/catalog/ma/2025.
; Form 1 line 2a: the personal exemption for the filing status.
(def ma-personal-exemption ((y MassachusettsYear) (status fed/FilingStatus)) Money :cite ((law "M.G.L. c. 62" "3")) (cond ((state-joint? status) (. y 'personal_exemption_joint)) ((or (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE)) (. y 'personal_exemption_hoh)) (else (. y 'personal_exemption_single))))

; Form 1 line 11: Social Security, Medicare and retirement contributions one
; person paid, from W-2 boxes 4 and 6, at most the cap.
(def ma-retirement-contributions ((y MassachusettsYear) (docs ret/Documents) (person-id String)) Money :cite ((law "M.G.L. c. 62" "3")) (min (. y 'retirement_contribution_cap) (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (if (is (. w 'person) person-id) (+ (. w 'form.social_security_tax_withheld) (. w 'form.medicare_tax_withheld)) #usd"0.00")) (. docs 'w2s))))

(def ma-w2-withheld ((docs ret/Documents)) Money :cite ((law "M.G.L. c. 62B" "2")) (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (sum (fn ((sw common/StateTaxWithholding)) Money (if (is (. sw 'state) "MA") (. sw 'tax_withheld) #usd"0.00")) (. w 'form.state_tax_withholding))) (. docs 'w2s)))

; Form 1 line 22: the tax on taxable 5.0% income. At or below the table limit
; it is read from the tax table, which taxes the middle of each $50 band at
; 5.0% and rounds to the dollar; income under $10 owes nothing. Above the
; limit it is line 21 times 5.0%.
(def ma-tax-on-taxable-income ((y MassachusettsYear) (taxable Money)) Money :cite ((law "M.G.L. c. 62" "4")) (withs (ti (clamp-zero taxable) rate (int-to-float (. y 'rate_bp))) (cond ((< ti #usd"10.00") #usd"0.00") ((<= ti #usd"50.00") #usd"1.00") ((<= ti (. y 'tax_table_limit)) (withs (steps (floor-float (/ (- ti #usd"0.01") #usd"50.00")) band-floor (* #usd"50.00" steps) midpoint (+ band-floor #usd"25.00")) (round-dollar (/ (* midpoint rate) 10000.0)))) (else (round-dollar (/ (* ti rate) 10000.0))))))

; An amount times a rate in basis points, rounded to the dollar.
(def ma-at-rate ((amount Money) (rate-bp Int)) Money :cite ((law "M.G.L. c. 62" "4")) (round-dollar (/ (* (clamp-zero amount) (int-to-float rate-bp)) 10000.0)))

; Massachusetts's estimated tax: M.G.L. c. 62B §§ 13 and 14, worked through on
; Form M-2210. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed massachusettstaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/MA.json.gz holds.
;
; The shape is federal: the lesser of a share of this year's tax and all of
; last year's, four equal installments, simple interest on each shortfall.
; The numbers are not: 80% rather than 90%, 100% of last year's tax at every
; income, a $400 threshold, annualised percentages of 20%, 40%, 60% and 80%,
; and a rate set each quarter. The figures follow the department's forms, the
; 2026 Form 1-ES and Form M-2210, and the answer's divergences say where c.
; 62B reads otherwise. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the 2026 Form 1-ES prints them.
(defstruct MassachusettsEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (floor Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (later_groups (Slice Date)))

(deffigures ma-estimated-2026 MassachusettsEstimatedYear 2026 (from ma-dor-form-1-es-2026 (floor #usd"400.00" :at who-must-pay) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at when-due) (later_groups (slice #date"2026-04-01" #date"2026-06-01" #date"2026-09-01") :at liability-changes)))

; A tax year's rules: its figures, and what Form M-2210, TIR 26-5 and M.G.L.
; c. 4 § 7 give it.
(defstruct MassachusettsEstimatedRules (figures MassachusettsEstimatedYear) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (holidays (Slice Date)) (stop Date) (last_charged Date) (period_ends (Slice Date)) (annualised_shares (Slice Int)) (rates (Slice EstRate)) (quarter_starts (Slice Date)) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

(= ma-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Massachusetts expects estimated payments if over $400 is due after withholding. The penalty is simple interest on each quarter's shortfall, at a quarterly rate." (slice "You avoid the penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 80% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. Last year's figure needs a return you filed for a full twelve-month year. It stays at 100% however high your income. The 4% surtax on income over $1,107,750 is part of the tax to cover." "The payments are four equal quarters. They're due April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A weekend or Massachusetts legal holiday shifts a date to the next business day. None of the 2026 dates is shifted. Withholding counts as paid in equal parts on the four dates. You can instead show when it was actually withheld. Filing your return early does not replace the January payment. You may only learn after March 31 that you must pay. The department's instructions then spread the year's amount over the dates left." "Tax after credits and withholding of $400 or less this year means no penalty. Nor is there one if you lived in Massachusetts all of last year and had no tax. Otherwise the penalty is interest, not compounded, on each shortfall. It runs from the due date until paid or April 15 of the next year. The rate is the federal short-term rate plus four points. That's 7% from April to June 2026 and 8% after. Form M-2210's annualised method can lower early quarters for late income. The department can waive the penalty for a casualty or disaster. It can also waive it for retiring after 62 or disability, with reasonable cause.") "Massachusetts uses 80% of this year's tax, not 90%. It uses 100% of last year's at every income, with no 110% tier. The threshold is $400, not $1,000. The annualised percentages are 20%, 40%, 60% and 80%. There's no relief for filing and paying by January 31. The rate is the federal short-term rate plus four points, set each quarter. The retirement waiver needs age 62." (slice "M.G.L. c. 62B §§ 13, 14; c. 62C § 32(a); c. 4 § 7, clause Eighteenth" "Form 1-ES, Massachusetts Estimated Income Tax, 2026" "Form M-2210, Underpayment of Massachusetts Estimated Income Tax, and its instructions, 2025, and the draft 2026 Form M-2210" "AP 241, Estimated Income Tax Payments (01/29/2025)" "TIR 26-5, Interest Rate on Overpayments and Underpayments (09/01/2026)")))

; The 2026 rules. The 80% and 100% tests, the line arithmetic, the April 15
; stop and Part 3's periods and percentages are Form M-2210's for 2025, which
; the draft 2026 form repeats with the 2026 dates; the rates are TIR 26-5's,
; and the rate from January 1, 2027 isn't published, so the penalty stops
; being rated there and says so. The holidays are M.G.L. c. 4 § 7, clause
; Eighteenth's, Bunker Hill Day in Suffolk county only; no 2026 due date
; falls on one. A figure's source must be for its year, and these sources

; Maryland's estimated tax: Md. Code, Tax-General §§ 10-815, 10-820, 10-902,
; 13-602 and 13-604, worked through on Form 502UP, Maryland's own
; underpayment form. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed marylandtaxcalc, whose answers golden/testdata/estimated/MD.json.gz
; holds.
;
; The outline is federal: 90% of this year's tax, four quarters, nothing at
; $500 or less after withholding. What differs, and makes Form 502UP a form
; of its own: last year's figure is 110% at every income; withholding counts
; on the dates it was withheld; the columns are running totals, so a
; shortfall still unpaid is charged again in every later column; uneven
; income takes the share of the year's income received by each period's end
; (lines 11 to 13), not annualised tax; and the charge is interest at the
; Comptroller's rate for the calendar year, by the month or part of a month
; (§ 13-604(a)). County tax is part of the tax throughout.
;
; The figures follow the 2026 Payment Voucher Worksheet and Form 502UP for
; 2025, the latest published; the answer's divergences say where the

; rules carry.

That tax is Maryland and county tax less Maryland withholding. The charge for paying too little is interest on each quarter's shortfall." (slice "Maryland charges nothing when your tax after withholding is $500 or less. Otherwise, withholding and estimated payments must reach a target. Short of it, interest is due. The target is 90% of this year's Maryland and local tax. If 110% of last year's tax is less, that is the target. The 110% applies at every income; there's no 100% figure as there is federally. County income tax is paid with the state's, so the payments have to cover both." "A quarter of the target is due by April 15, June 15 and September 15. The last quarter is due by January 15 of the next year. A date on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next business day. Withholding counts on the dates it was taken, not spread evenly over the year. Late-year withholding doesn't cover an early quarter. Filing your return and paying in full by January 31 replaces January's payment. If your income came unevenly, there's another way to measure each quarter. Use the share of the year's income you'd received by then." "Interest is figured on what was short at each due date. An earlier shortfall still unpaid counts again at every later date. Interest runs until the shortfall is paid or the return is due on April 15. The rate is set for each calendar year: 10.8133% for 2026 and 9.995% for 2027. Interest is charged by the month, and part of a month counts as a whole one. The Comptroller may waive the interest for reasonable cause. The law also allows a separate penalty of up to 25% of the shortfall. The underpayment form doesn't figure that penalty.") "Maryland differs from federal rules in six ways. Its $500 threshold counts county tax. Everyone uses 110% of last year's tax. Withholding counts on its dates. Uneven income uses the share of the year's income received, not annualizing. A shortfall is charged again at every later quarter. The yearly rate has a 9% floor and is charged by the month." ; Maine's estimated tax: 36 M.R.S. § 5228, with the interest of § 186,
; worked through on Form 2210ME, Maine's own underpayment form. It is written
; on the shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and
; reproduces the Go rules in the removed mainetaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/ME.json.gz holds.
;
; Maine differs from the federal rules in shape. No payments are needed if
; either this year's tax after withholding or last year's liability is under
; $1,000. There is no 110% tier. Instead, income not subject to Maine
; withholding that is $500,000 or more above the same period of last year is
; an "unusual event": 90% of the tax on it is due with that period's
; installment, and last year's liability does not cover it. The penalty is
; interest under § 186, charged by the month, a part of a month counting as
; a whole one, and compounded monthly.
;
; The figures follow § 5228 and Form 2210ME (2025), the latest penalty form;
; the answer's divergences say where § 5228 reads otherwise. The 2027 rate is
; not published, so the months beginning after December 31, 2026 are not
; charged and the penalty says so. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.

; How Maine's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these rules
; carry.
(= me-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Maine expects estimated payments when two figures are both $1,000 or more. They are your tax after withholding this year and last year's tax. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall, counted in whole months." (slice "You avoid the penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the lesser of 90% of this year's Maine tax or 100% of last year's. Last year can set it only if it was a full 12-month year. There's no higher figure for high incomes. Maine asks for nothing if this year's tax after withholding is under $1,000. It also asks for nothing if last year's tax was under $1,000." "The exception is a sudden jump in income without Maine withholding. A rise of $500,000 or more on the same part of last year is an \"unusual event\". That quarter's payment must include 90% of the tax on the extra income. Last year's tax doesn't cover it, even when that tax was under $1,000." "A quarter is due April 15, June 15 and September 15, 2026, and January 15, 2027. A date on a weekend or Maine holiday is due the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly across the four dates. You can file and pay in full by the end of January. Then there's no penalty on the January payment. For 2026, the end of January is Monday, February 1, 2027." "The penalty is interest at 0.75% a month for 2026, compounded monthly. A part of a month counts as a whole one. A payment one day late costs a full month. It runs until the shortfall is paid or the return is due on April 15. The annualized worksheet can lower early payments for uneven income. The assessor may waive the penalty for cause.") "Federal needs no payments only if last year's tax was zero. Maine needs none if it was under $1,000. Maine has no 110% tier. A $500,000 income jump without withholding has 90% of its tax due that quarter. That holds whatever last year's tax was. The penalty is charged by the month, compounded monthly, at a fixed annual rate." ; Michigan's estimated income tax: MCL 206.301 with the interest and
; penalties of MCL 205.23 and 205.24, worked through on Form MI-2210,
; Michigan's own underpayment form. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed michigantaxcalc, whose answers golden/testdata/estimated/MI.json.gz
; holds.
;
; MCL 206.301(11) adopts the federal computation of the installments and of
; the period of underpayment, so the required payment, the quarters and the
; interest period look federal. The charge does not. Michigan charges two
; things on each quarter's shortfall: interest by the day at a factor
; Treasury prints for each half-year, in whole dollars, and a flat penalty of
; 25% or 10% with $25 and $10 minimums. The two are figured on different
; underpayments: interest applies a later payment to the oldest shortfall
; first (MI-2210 Part 2), and the penalty counts a payment only in the
; quarter it arrives (Part 3).
;
; The figures follow Treasury's forms, the 2026 MI-1040ES and the 2025
; MI-2210, the latest published, and the answer's divergences say where the
; statutes read otherwise. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as MCL 206.301 sets them.
(defstruct MichiganEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)))

; The 2026 figures.
(deffigures mi-estimated-2026 MichiganEstimatedYear 2026 (from mi-legis-mcl-206-301-2026 (threshold #usd"500.00" :at subsection-1) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at subsection-1)))

; How Michigan's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= mi-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Michigan expects estimated payments when more than $500 will be due. The $500 is measured after withholding and credits. Falling short costs interest on each quarter's shortfall. A flat penalty of 10% or 25% of that shortfall is added." (slice "You are clear if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. It is the lesser of 90% of this year's Michigan tax or 100% of last year's. Last year's figure is 110% when its adjusted gross income was over $150,000. The limit is $75,000 if last year's return was married filing separately. Last year's figure also needs a return you filed for a full 12 months." "The payments are four equal quarters. They are due April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15 of the next year. A date on a weekend or legal holiday shifts to the next business day. Withholding counts a quarter on each date, unless you show when it was taken. Form MI-2210's annualised worksheet can lower early quarters for uneven income." "Interest runs by the day on each quarter's shortfall from its due date. It stops when the shortfall is paid, or on April 15 of the next year. Treasury sets the rate each January and July at one point above the prime rate. A later payment pays the oldest shortfall first. For the flat penalty, a payment counts only for the quarter in which it arrives. Catching up later stops the interest but not the penalty. It is 25% of the shortfall, at least $25, for a quarter with nothing paid. It is 10%, at least $10, for a quarter paid short." "This year's tax after withholding and credits may be $500 or less. If so, nothing is charged. Nothing is charged if last year's return covered 12 months and showed no tax. No flat penalty applies if last year needed no estimated payments or no return. Interest can still be due. You can file and pay in full by the end of January. That removes the January quarter's penalty but not its interest. Treasury waives the penalty for reasonable cause shown in a written request. That waiver doesn't cover interest. After a declared disaster, Treasury can waive both for people who ask. There is no waiver for retirement or disability.") "Michigan follows the federal required payment, quarters and interest period. Its threshold is $500 rather than $1,000. It adds a flat 10% or 25% penalty on each quarter's shortfall to the interest. That penalty is figured without applying later payments to earlier quarters. The interest rate is prime plus one point, set twice a year. There is no waiver for retirement or disability." (slice "MCL 206.301; MCL 205.23(2) to (4); MCL 205.24(6); MCL 8.6" "2026 MI-1040ES, Michigan Estimated Income Tax for Individuals (Rev. 04-25)" "2025 MI-2210, Underpayment of Estimated Income Tax, and its instructions (Rev. 10-25)" "Revenue Administrative Bulletin 2021-17, Estimated Payments for Individuals and Fiduciaries" "Revenue Administrative Bulletins 2026-5 and 2026-10 (interest rates)" "Revenue Administrative Bulletin 2025-15, Penalty Provisions")))

; Form M1, Minnesota Individual Income Tax, for a full-year resident.
;
; The return starts from the prepared federal return: federal AGI, the federal
; filing status and the dependents it claims. The schedules that feed it are
; taken as inputs: Schedule M1M's additions and subtractions, Schedule M1SA's
; itemized deductions, Schedule M1C's nonrefundable credits, and the
; refundable credits of Schedule M1REF, among them the Child and Working
; Family Credits of Schedule M1CWFC.
;
; The rules cite the law (Minn. Stat. ch. 290). The parts of the form and
; instructions they implement name them in sources/catalog/mn/2025.
; The standard deduction before the income limitation: the Standard Deduction
; Table for Line 4, or for a filer someone else can claim, the Worksheet for
; Line 4 — Dependent Standard Deduction.
(defworksheet mn-basic-standard-deduction ((y MinnesotaYear) (status fed/FilingStatus) (boxes Int) (claimable Bool) (earned-income Money)) Money :cite ((law "Minn. Stat." "290.0123")) (bind married (or (state-joint? status) (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_SEPARATELY) (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE))) (line 1 "Basic standard deduction for the filing status" (cond ((or (state-joint? status) (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE)) (. y 'standard_deduction_joint)) ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) (. y 'standard_deduction_hoh)) (else (. y 'standard_deduction_single)))) (line 2 "Additional amount for each box checked for age 65 or older and blind" (* boxes (if married (. y 'standard_deduction_additional_married) (. y 'standard_deduction_additional_unmarried)))) (line 3 "Standard deduction from the table" (+ line1 line2)) (line 4 "Dependent standard deduction: the greater of $1,250 and earned income plus $350, but no more than line 3" (min line3 (max #usd"1250.00" (+ (clamp-zero earned-income) #usd"350.00")))) (result (if claimable line4 line3)))

; Worksheets A and B for Line 4 — Standard Deduction Limitation.
(defworksheet mn-standard-deduction ((y MinnesotaYear) (status fed/FilingStatus) (agi Money) (basic Money)) Money :cite ((law "Minn. Stat." "290.0123")) (bind separate (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_SEPARATELY)) (bind lower (if separate (/ (. y 'deduction_limit_threshold) 2.0) (. y 'deduction_limit_threshold))) (bind upper (if separate (/ (. y 'deduction_limit_upper_threshold) 2.0) (. y 'deduction_limit_upper_threshold))) (line 1 "Adjusted gross income from line 1 of Form M1" agi) (line 2 "Income over the first threshold, up to the second" (clamp-zero (- (min line1 upper) lower))) (line 3 "Multiply step 2 by 3%" (round-dollar (/ (* line2 (int-to-float (. y 'deduction_limit_low_rate_bp))) 10000.0))) (line 4 "Income over the second threshold" (clamp-zero (- line1 upper))) (line 5 "Multiply step 4 by 10%" (round-dollar (/ (* line4 (int-to-float (. y 'deduction_limit_high_rate_bp))) 10000.0))) (line 6 "Add steps 3 and 5" (+ line3 line5)) (line 7 "Standard deduction before the limitation" basic) (line 8 "Multiply step 7 by 80%" (round-dollar (/ (* line7 (int-to-float (. y 'deduction_limit_max_bp))) 10000.0))) (line 9 "The lesser of step 6 and step 8" (min line6 line8)) (line 10 "Standard deduction: step 7 minus step 9" (- line7 line9)) (result line10))

; Worksheet for Line 5 — Dependent Exemptions.
(defworksheet mn-dependent-exemptions ((y MinnesotaYear) (status fed/FilingStatus) (agi Money) (dependents Int) (claimable Bool)) Money :cite ((law "Minn. Stat." "290.0121")) (bind separate (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_SEPARATELY)) (bind range (if separate (/ (. y 'exemption_phaseout_range) 2.0) (. y 'exemption_phaseout_range))) (bind step (if separate (/ (. y 'exemption_phaseout_step) 2.0) (. y 'exemption_phaseout_step))) (line 3 "Number of dependents multiplied by $5,200" (* dependents (. y 'dependent_exemption))) (line 4 "Adjusted gross income from line 1 of Form M1" agi) (line 5 "Threshold for the filing status" (cond ((or (state-joint? status) (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE)) (. y 'exemption_threshold_joint)) ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) (. y 'exemption_threshold_hoh)) (separate (. y 'exemption_threshold_separate)) (else (. y 'exemption_threshold_single)))) (line 6 "Income over the threshold" (clamp-zero (- line4 line5))) (bind steps (ceil-float (/ (money-to-float line6) (money-to-float step)))) (line 9 "Reduction: 2% of step 3 for each step of income over the threshold" (round-dollar (/ (* line3 (* steps (int-to-float (. y 'exemption_phaseout_step_rate_bp)))) 10000.0))) (line 10 "Dependent exemptions: step 3 minus step 9" (cond (claimable #usd"0.00") ((> line6 range) #usd"0.00") (else (clamp-zero (- line3 line9))))) (result line10))

; Line 10: the tax from the tax table below $86,800 of taxable income, which
; taxes the middle of each $100 band (the first two bands are $0 to $20, taxed
; nothing, and $20 to $100, taxed as $60), or from the rate schedules above it.
(def mn-tax ((y MinnesotaYear) (status fed/FilingStatus) (taxable Money)) Money :cite ((law "Minn. Stat." "290.06")) (withs (rows (mn-schedule status) ti (clamp-zero taxable) figured (cond ((>= ti (. y 'tax_table_limit)) ti) ((< ti #usd"20.00") #usd"0.00") ((< ti #usd"100.00") #usd"60.00") (else (+ (float-to-money (* (floor-float (/ (money-to-float ti) 100.0)) 100.0)) #usd"50.00")))) (round-dollar (state-bracket-tax rows figured false))))

; Minnesota's estimated tax: Minn. Stat. § 289A.25, with the rate under
; § 270C.40, worked through on Schedule M15, which follows federal Form 2210
; line for line. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed minnesotataxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/MN.json.gz holds.
;
; Minnesota follows the federal shape: four 25% instalments, the lesser of 90%
; of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, and 110% above $150,000 of last
; year's AGI. It differs in the $500 threshold, the single rate fixed for the
; whole tax year, refundable credits counted as payments, and the
; no-liability exception, which needs a full year of Minnesota residence. The
; figures follow the 2026 Schedule M15, marked "FINAL DRAFT — 10/1/26", and
; the answer's divergences say where the statute reads otherwise. A year with
; no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Schedule M15 and its instructions for the year
; print them.
(defstruct MinnesotaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (high_income_rate Int) (high_income_agi Money) (nonresident_minimum Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (shares (Slice Int)) (period_ends (Slice Date)) (annualised_shares (Slice Int)) (file_and_pay_by Date) (deemed_paid Date) (stop Date) (rates (Slice EstRate)))

; The 2026 figures. § 270C.40 subd. 4 takes the rate for January 1, 2026 for
; every day of a 2026 underpayment, including the days in 2027, so the rate
; runs to April 15, 2027 and no later one is needed.
(deffigures mn-estimated-2026 MinnesotaEstimatedYear 2026 (from mn-dor-schedule-m15-2026 (threshold #usd"500.00" :at line-3) (this_year_rate 9000 :at line-4) (last_year_rate 10000 :at line-5) (high_income_rate 11000 :at line-5) (high_income_agi #usd"150000.00" :at line-5) (nonresident_minimum #usd"1.00" :at avoid-the-penalty) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at line-13) (shares (slice 2500 2500 2500 2500) :at line-13) (period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :at annualized-worksheet) (annualised_shares (slice 2250 4500 6750 9000) :at annualized-worksheet) (file_and_pay_by #date"2027-01-31" :at line-14) (deemed_paid #date"2027-01-15" :at line-14) (stop #date"2027-04-15" :at line-17) (rates (slice (EstRate #date"2026-01-01" #date"2027-04-15" 70000 "Minn. Stat. § 270C.40 subd. 4; 2026 Schedule M15, line 20: 7% for tax year 2026")) :at line-20)))

; A tax year's rules: its figures, and how they are explained.
(defstruct MinnesotaEstimatedRules (figures MinnesotaEstimatedYear) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How Minnesota's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= mn-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Minnesota expects estimated payments once $500 or more would be due. That figure is after withholding and refundable credits. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall. It uses one rate for the year, 7% for 2026." (slice "Withholding, refundable credits and estimated payments count toward a target. It is the smaller of 90% of this year's Minnesota tax or 100% of last year's. Reaching it keeps you clear of the penalty. Last year's figure becomes 110% if last year's federal AGI was over $150,000. There is no lower figure for married filing separately. Last year's figure needs a full-year return that showed some Minnesota tax." "The payments are a quarter each. They are due April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15 of the next year. Withholding and refundable credits count as paid evenly across those dates. This holds unless you show when they were actually paid. A return filed with the tax paid by January 31 counts as paid on January 15." "No penalty is due if this year's tax less withholding and credits is under $500. The same holds if you had no Minnesota tax last year and lived there all of it. If the IRS waives your federal penalty, Minnesota does too. That covers retiring, becoming disabled, a casualty or a disaster." "The penalty is figured by the day on Schedule M15. It runs from each due date until the shortfall is paid in full. It stops on April 15 of the next year. The rate is set once from the prime rate and holds for the whole tax year. An annualized method can lower early payments if income comes late in the year.") "Minnesota's threshold is $500, not $1,000. The $150,000 step has no $75,000 figure for married filing separately. Refundable credits count as payments spread over the year. The no-liability exception needs a full year of Minnesota residence. One rate covers the whole tax year. A return filed by January 31 counts as paid on January 15." (slice "Minn. Stat. §§ 289A.25, 270C.40, 270C.395, 645.151" "2026 Schedule M15 and its instructions (final draft, October 1, 2026)" "Minnesota Department of Revenue, Estimated Tax Payments for Individuals (updated January 7, 2026)" "Minnesota Department of Revenue, Penalties and Interest for Individuals (interest rate table)")))

(= mn-estimated-years (Table Int MinnesotaEstimatedRules) (table 2026 mn-estimated-rules-2026))

; Missouri's estimated tax: RSMo §§ 143.521, 143.531 and 143.761, with the
; rate under § 32.065, worked through on Form MO-2210, Missouri's own
; underpayment form. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed missouritaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/MO.json.gz holds.
;
; Missouri keeps the federal rules of the 1980s. The required annual payment
; is the lesser of 90% of this year's tax and 100% of last year's, with no
; 110% tier. What makes MO-2210 a form of its own is Section B: four
; exceptions that each excuse an instalment whose payments reach them, last
; year's tax, last year's income at this year's rates, 90% of the tax on
; annualized income and 90% of the tax on income to date. A late starter
; pays fewer, larger instalments, and each column's running underpayment is
; charged by the day at each calendar year's rate.
;
; The figures follow Form MO-1040ES for 2026 and Form MO-2210 for 2025, the
; latest penalty form, with its dates a year on; the answer's divergences say
; where § 143.761 reads otherwise. Kansas City's and St. Louis's earnings
; taxes are collected by the cities and are not covered. A year with no
; figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Form MO-1040ES for the year and the
; department's interest rate page print them.

; The 2026 figures. The page's 7% for 2026 is the emergency amendment of
; 12 CSR 10-41.010; the rate for 2027 is posted too, so every day to April
; 15, 2027 is rated.

; How Missouri's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= mo-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Missouri expects estimated payments once $100 or more is due after withholding. Its penalty form charges nothing under $500. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall. The rate is set each calendar year, 7% for 2026 and 2027." (slice "Your target is 90% of this year's Missouri tax or 100% of last year's. It is whichever is smaller. You're clear if withholding and estimated payments cover a quarter by each date. The dates are April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. There is no 110% figure for higher incomes. Last year's figure counts only from a twelve-month return that showed tax. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates. You can instead show when it was taken." "Missouri also excuses a quarter when payments so far reach one of four measures. Two are last year's tax and last year's income taxed at this year's rates. The other two are 90% of the tax on your income to date, annualized or actual. The last two do not apply to the January payment." "If you first had to pay later in the year, you pay fewer, larger installments. That is three from June 15, two from September 15, or one in January. A return filed and paid by January 31 counts as paid on January 15. The interest runs by the day from each due date until paid or April 15. Missouri does not waive it for reasonable cause.") "Missouri's prior-year test is always 100% and needs a return that showed tax. Last year's income at this year's rates is still a safe harbor. The annualized and to-date income tests excuse a quarter rather than lower it. They do not apply to the fourth. A late starter has fewer installments. The rate is set each calendar year. There is no waiver for casualty, retirement or disability." (slice "RSMo §§ 143.521, 143.531, 143.761, 32.065" "Form MO-2210, 2025 Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, and its instructions" "Form MO-1040ES, 2026 Declaration of Estimated Tax for Individuals (Revised 12-2025)" "12 CSR 10-41.010 (emergency amendment, 2026 rate); Missouri DOR, Statutory Interest Rates" "12 CSR 10-2.067")))

; The 2026 rules. The 2026 MO-2210 is not published, so its figures are the

; and the April 15 stop. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are
; written out rather than deffigures. The 2025 form prints January 31, 2026,

; Mississippi's estimated tax: Miss. Code § 27-7-327 and 35 Miss. Admin.
; Code Pt. III, Subpt. 11, Ch. 21, R. 100, worked through on Form 80-320,
; Mississippi's own interest and penalty worksheet. It is written on the
; shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and
; reproduces the Go rules in the removed mississippitaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/MS.json.gz holds.
;
; Mississippi differs from the federal rules in shape. The current-year test
; is 80%, and the prior-year test is 100% with no higher tier. All
; withholding counts toward the April instalment. What makes Form 80-320 a
; form of its own is the charge: interest of ½% a month on the running
; underestimate, column by column, from each due date to the next or until
; paid, the fourth column running to April 15.
;
; The figures follow Rule 100 and Form 80-320 (Rev. 09/25), the latest
; published; no 2026 edition is posted. The answer's divergences say where
; the form, the rule and the statute part ways. No source says whether a due
; date on a weekend or holiday moves, and every 2026 date and April 15, 2027
; are weekdays, so none is moved; no source states a January 31 file-and-pay
; rule, so there is none. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Rule 100 prints them for the year.

; Montana's estimated tax: Mont. Code Ann. § 15-30-2512, with the rate under
; § 15-1-216(7), worked through on Form EST-I, which follows federal Form 2210
; line for line. Montana calls the charge interest on underpayment of
; estimated tax. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed montanataxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/MT.json.gz holds.
;
; Montana follows the federal shape: four 25% instalments, the lesser of 90%
; of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, and payments applied to the
; earliest instalment first. It differs in the $500 threshold, no 110% tier,
; a full exemption for farmers and ranchers and for anybody who retired after
; 62 or became disabled this year or last, and one rate for the whole tax
; year: the rate in effect when the return is due, so 2027's for 2026. The
; figures follow Form EST-I for 2025, the latest published, with the 2026
; dates, and the answer's divergences say where the statute reads otherwise.
; Not built: the hardship extension of § 15-30-2512(7), which the department
; grants on a written request, and short tax years. A year with no figures is
; answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Publication 1 for the year prints them.
(defstruct MontanaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (shares (Slice Int)))

; North Carolina's estimated tax: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-163.15, with the
; rate under § 105-241.21, worked through on Form D-422, which follows federal
; Form 2210 line for line. North Carolina calls the charge interest. It is
; written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed northcarolinataxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/NC.json.gz holds.
;
; North Carolina follows the federal rules closely: four 25% instalments, the
; lesser of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, the $1,000
; threshold the statute takes from 26 U.S.C. § 6654(e), and payments applied
; to the earliest instalment first. It has no 110% tier, a no-liability
; exception with no twelve-month or residence condition, no waiver for
; casualty, retirement or disability, and a rate the Secretary sets for each
; half-year. The figures follow Form D-422 for 2025, the latest published,
; with the 2026 dates and rates; the answer's divergences say where the
; statute reads otherwise. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Form NC-40 for the year and the department's
; interest rate page print them.
(defstruct NorthCarolinaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (shares (Slice Int)) (rates (Slice EstRate)))

; The 2026 figures. The rate from January 1, 2027 isn't published: the rates
; end on December 31, 2026, and the interest says so.
(deffigures nc-estimated-2026 NorthCarolinaEstimatedYear 2026 (from nc-dor-form-nc-40-2026 (threshold #usd"1000.00" :at who-must-pay) (this_year_rate 9000 :at interest) (last_year_rate 10000 :at interest) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at when-to-pay) (shares (slice 2500 2500 2500 2500) :at interest)) (from nc-dor-interest-rate-2026 (rates (slice (EstRate #date"2026-01-01" #date"2026-12-31" 70000 "NCDOR, Interest Rate: 7% for January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026, and for July 1 through December 31, 2026")) :at rates-2026)))

; A tax year's rules: its figures, and what Form D-422 and the statute give
; it.
(defstruct NorthCarolinaEstimatedRules (figures NorthCarolinaEstimatedYear) (period_ends (Slice Date)) (annualised_shares (Slice Int)) (file_and_pay_by Date) (deemed_paid Date) (stop Date) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How North Carolina's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years
; these rules carry.
(= nc-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "North Carolina expects estimated payments if $1,000 or more of tax would be due. That is the tax left after withholding and credits. Falling short costs interest, 7% a year for 2026, on each quarter's shortfall." (slice "You're clear if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. A quarter is due by each of April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. There is no 110% figure for higher incomes. Last year's figure needs a full-year return you filed. Withholding counts as paid evenly unless you show when it was taken." "There is no interest if this year's tax less withholding is under $1,000. Nor is there any if you had no North Carolina income tax liability last year. A return filed with the balance paid by January 31 counts in the January column. It counts as paid on January 15." "The interest runs by the day from each due date until the shortfall is paid. It stops on April 15 of the next year. Each payment goes first to the oldest shortfall. The Secretary of Revenue sets the rate for each half-year. North Carolina has no waiver for a casualty, retirement or disability. Annualizing can lower early payments when income arrives late in the year.") "Unlike federal, there is no 110% tier. The no-liability exception has no twelve-month or residence condition. There is no waiver for casualty, retirement or disability. The state sets the rate each half-year. A return filed by January 31 counts as paid on January 15. The $1,000 threshold is the federal one." (slice "N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 105-163.15, 105-241.21, 105-237" "Form D-422, 2025 Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, and its instructions" "Form NC-40, Individual Estimated Income Tax (for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026)" "NCDOR, Interest Rate; Estimated Income Tax")))

; The 2026 rules. Form D-422 for 2026 is not published, so the D-422 and
; D-422A figures are the 2025 forms', with the 2026 dates: the annualised
; periods and shares, the January 31 rule and the April 15 stop. A figure's
; source must be for its year, so these are written out rather than
; deffigures. No North Carolina holiday is listed: the four 2026 due dates
; are weekdays.
(= nc-estimated-rules-2026 NorthCarolinaEstimatedRules (make-struct NorthCarolinaEstimatedRules :figures nc-estimated-2026 :period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :annualised_shares (slice 2250 4500 6750 9000) :file_and_pay_by #date"2027-01-31" :deemed_paid #date"2027-01-15" :stop #date"2027-04-15" :explanation nc-estimated-explanation))

(= nc-estimated-years (Table Int NorthCarolinaEstimatedRules) (table 2026 nc-estimated-rules-2026))

; The form the worksheet holds.
(= nc-estimated-form String "Form D-422, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals")

; "Jan 15" inside the tax year and "Jan 15, 2027" outside it, as the Go
; rules' shortDate writes a date.
(def nc-short-date ((d Date) (year Int)) String :cite () (if (is (date-year d) year) (concat (slice (elt est-short-month-names (- (date-month d) 1)) " " (int-to-string (date-day d)))) (est-short-date d)))

; What tax less withholding leaves, as a sentence for a requirement's why.
(def nc-owed-why ((tax Money) (withheld Money)) String :cite () (if (is withheld #usd"0.00") (concat (slice "Your North Carolina tax is " (est-whole tax) ", with no withholding.")) (concat (slice "North Carolina tax of " (est-whole tax) " less " (est-whole withheld) " withheld " (est-leaves (- tax withheld)) "."))))

; What the target leaves to pay after withholding, for a why.
(def nc-target-why ((target Money) (withheld Money)) String :cite () (if (is withheld #usd"0.00") (concat (slice "Your target is " (est-whole target) ", a quarter by each due date.")) (concat (slice "Your target is " (est-whole target) ", which leaves " (est-whole (- target withheld)) " after withholding. Pay a quarter of that by each due date."))))

; What estimated payments the target leaves after withholding, for a why.
(def nc-left-why ((target Money) (withheld Money)) String :cite () (if (is withheld #usd"0.00") (concat (slice "That's " (est-whole target) " of estimated payments, a quarter by each due date.")) (concat (slice "After " (est-whole withheld) " of withholding, you need " (est-whole (- target withheld)) " of estimated payments. Pay a quarter by each due date."))))

; North Dakota's estimated tax: N.D.C.C. §§ 57-38-62 and 57-38-63, with the
; interest under § 57-38-45, worked through on Schedule ND-1UT, North
; Dakota's own underpayment form. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed northdakotataxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/ND.json.gz holds. North Dakota calls the charge
; interest.
;
; Estimates are owed only by someone who must also pay federal estimated
; tax, and only when last year's North Dakota net tax liability was $1,000 or
; more. The required payment is the lesser of 90% of this year's tax or 100%
; of last year's, with no 110% tier and no twelve-month test, in four 25%
; instalments. What makes ND-1UT a form of its own: a payment goes first to
; its own quarter, and only the excess pays an earlier shortfall, as of that
; quarter's due date; and the interest, a fixed 12% a year, takes the days
; over 365 rounded to three places, times 12% rounded to three places again.
;
; Three facts come from the federal answer to the same request: whether
; federal estimates were required, whether the federal January instalment
; was excused, and whether the annualised method was used federally. Each is
; answered only when the request gives federal figures.
;
; The figures follow Form ND-1ES for 2026 and Schedule ND-1UT for 2025, the
; latest published, with the 2026 dates; the answer's divergences say where
; the forms and the statute part ways. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Form ND-1ES for the year prints them.

; Nebraska's estimated tax: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 77-2769 and 77-2790 and 316
; Neb. Admin. Code ch. 20, with the rate under § 45-104.02, worked through on
; Form 2210N, which follows federal Form 2210 line for line. It is written on
; the shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and
; reproduces the Go rules in the removed nebraskataxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/NE.json.gz holds.
;
; Nebraska follows the federal rules: four 25% instalments, the lesser of 90%
; of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, 110% above $150,000 of last
; year's federal AGI, and payments applied to the earliest instalment first.
; It differs in the $500 threshold, an exception for first-time filers, and
; the rate: the delinquent tax rate under § 45-104.02, 8% a year, simple. The
; figures follow the 2026 Form 2210N, and the answer's divergences say where
; the statute or the regulation reads otherwise. Line 22a of Form 2210N
; charges "the number of days in 2026 on line 21" and line 22b is reserved;
; Revenue Ruling 99-26-2 keeps 8% through 2028, so every day is charged at 8%
; whichever line it falls on. Not built: tax paid for a nonresident by a
; pass-through entity or fiduciary, which REG-20-007.05 counts on the last day
; of the entity's year; a caller gives it as a dated payment. A year with no
; figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Form 2210N for the year and the department's
; interest rate ruling print them.

; New Jersey's estimated gross income tax: N.J.S.A. 54A:8-4, 54A:8-5 and
; 54A:9-6(c) and (d), with interest under N.J.S.A. 54:49-3, worked through on
; Form NJ-2210, New Jersey's own underpayment form. It is written on the
; shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and
; reproduces the Go rules in the removed newjerseytaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/NJ.json.gz holds. New Jersey calls the charge
; interest.
;
; New Jersey keeps the older federal rules. The underpayment is measured
; against the lesser of 80% of this year's tax and 100% of last year's, a
; quarter by each date, with nothing under $400 of tax after withholding and
; credits. Four exceptions each take the interest off a quarter whose
; payments reach them: last year's tax, last year's income at this year's
; rates, 80% of the tax on annualized income, and 90% of the tax on income
; to date. Interest is prime plus 3% for each month or part of a month, 10%
; for 2026, which makes NJ-2210 a form of its own.
;
; The figures follow the 2026 Form NJ-1040-ES, TB-21(R) for the rate, and
; Form NJ-2210 for 2025, the latest penalty form, with the 2026 dates; the
; answer's divergences say where the statutes read otherwise. Option 2 of the
; NJ-2210 instructions counts each month or part of a month from the due
; date, and its rate schedule gives a month the rate of the period it starts
; in, so 10.00% covers the months that start through January 15, 2027. The
; rate after that is set from prime on December 1, 2026 and is not
; published: later months are not charged, and the penalty says so. Every due
; date is the fifteenth, so the months a quarter's balance runs line up with
; the due dates, and figuring each period's balance, as Option 1 does, gives
; Option 2's months.
;
; Not built, as in the Go rules: the exception for an instalment due on or
; after the taxpayer's death (§ 54A:9-6(c)); Form NJ-2210NR, which scales
; Exceptions 2 to 4 by a nonresident's income percentage, which a caller can
; apply to the amounts it gives; and estates and trusts. A year with no
; figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the year's Form NJ-1040-ES and TB-21(R) print
; them.
(defstruct NewJerseyEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (filing_threshold Money) (filing_threshold_single Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (file_and_pay_by Date) (rate Int) (rate_source String))

; How New Jersey's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= nj-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "New Jersey expects estimated payments above a $400 threshold. That's your tax after withholding and credits. Falling short costs interest at prime plus 3%, 10% for 2026. It's charged for each month or part of a month." (slice "Withholding, refundable credits and estimated payments must reach a target. The target is the smaller of 80% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. A quarter is due by April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. There is no 110% figure in practice. The Division charges interest only against those two amounts." "A quarter also avoids interest if payments so far reach one of four measures. The first is last year's tax. The second is the tax on last year's income at this year's rates. The third is 80% of the tax on your income annualized to date. The fourth is 90% of the tax on your actual income to date. The last two do not apply to January. Filing and paying in full by February 15 replaces the January payment." "Interest runs from each due date until the shortfall is paid. It stops on April 15 of the next year. Any part of a month counts as a whole month. Withholding and refundable credits count as paid a quarter on each date. You can show other dates instead. The Division cannot waive this interest for reasonable cause. Nor can it waive it for a casualty, retirement or disability.") "New Jersey's current-year test is 80% rather than 90%. Its threshold is $400 rather than $1,000, and the 110% tier never applies. Four exceptions excuse a quarter outright. Interest is charged by the month at prime plus 3%. Filing by February 15, not January 31, replaces the January payment. There is no casualty, retirement or disability waiver." (slice "N.J.S.A. 54A:8-4, 54A:8-5, 54A:9-6, 54:49-3, 54:49-11" "Form NJ-2210, 2025 Underpayment of Estimated Tax, and its instructions" "2026 Form NJ-1040-ES" "GIT-8, Estimating Income Taxes (January 2026)" "TB-21(R), Interest Rate Assessed on Tax Balances for 2026" "Notice Concerning Estimated Tax for Taxpayers Earning Over $150,000")))

; New Mexico's estimated tax: NMSA 1978 § 7-2-12.2, with the rate under
; § 7-1-67, worked through on Form RPD-41272. New Mexico calls the charge a
; penalty and figures it as interest. It is written on the shared machinery
; in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules
; in the removed newmexicotaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/NM.json.gz holds.
;
; New Mexico follows the federal shape: four 25% instalments, the lesser of
; 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, payments applied to the
; earliest instalment first, and the federal underpayment rate quarter by
; quarter. It differs in the $1,000 threshold, no 110% tier, a full exemption
; for first-year residents, a no-liability exception only for full-year
; residents, and a late start instead of an annualized method. The figures
; follow Form RPD-41272 for 2025, the latest published, with the 2026 dates
; and rates, and the answer's divergences say where the statute reads
; otherwise. The rate from January 1, 2027 is not published, so those days
; are not charged and the penalty says so. Not built: withholding under the
; Oil and Gas Proceeds and Pass-Through Entity Withholding Tax Act, which a
; caller gives with the rest; and the separate election for wage and other
; withholding, which here is one election for all of it. A year with no
; figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the department's rates page prints them.
(defstruct NewMexicoEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (rates (Slice EstRate)))

(deffigures nm-estimated-2026 NewMexicoEstimatedYear 2026 (from nm-trd-penalty-interest-rates-2026 (rates (slice (EstRate #date"2026-04-01" #date"2026-06-30" 60000 "Taxation and Revenue Department, Penalty Interest Rates: April 1, 2026 – June 30, 2026, 6%") (EstRate #date"2026-07-01" #date"2026-12-31" 70000 "Taxation and Revenue Department, Penalty Interest Rates: July 1, 2026 – December 31, 2026, 7%")) :at rates-2026)))

; rules carry.
(= nm-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "New Mexico expects estimated payments from anyone who files a return. It charges no penalty unless your tax less withholding is $1,000 or more. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall. It is charged at the federal underpayment rate." (slice "You are clear if withholding and estimated payments reach your target on time. It is the smaller of 90% of this year's New Mexico tax or 100% of last year's. A quarter is due by each of April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. There is no 110% figure for higher incomes. Last year's figure needs a full-year New Mexico return. Withholding counts as paid evenly unless you show when it was taken." "You need no estimated payments if last year's full-year return had no tax due. You must also have lived in New Mexico all of that year. Late income can mean you first have to pay after March 31. If so, you catch up at the next date instead. Pay half by June 15, three-quarters by September 15, or all of it by January 15. Filing and paying in full by January 31 clears the January payment's penalty." "The penalty runs daily from each due date until paid or the next April 15. Each payment goes first to the oldest shortfall. The rate follows the federal one quarter by quarter. It is 6% from April to June 2026 and 7% from July. The department can waive the penalty. That needs an underpayment not due to fraud or negligence.") "New Mexico has no 110% tier. The no-liability exception needs a full year of New Mexico residence. There is no annualized method. A late start catches up at the first date that applies. The first quarter's rate after the year also covers April 1 to 15." (slice "NMSA 1978 § 7-2-12.2, as amended by Laws 2011, HB 470" "Form RPD-41272, 2025 Calculation of Estimated Personal Income Tax Underpayment Penalty, and its instructions" "Instructions for PIT-ES, New Mexico Estimated Tax Payment Voucher" "Taxation and Revenue Department, Estimated Payments and Penalty Interest Rates")))

; Rate applied to an amount, rate in thousandths of a percent, to the cent.
(def ny-rate-of ((amount Money) (rate-pcm Int)) Money :cite ((law "N.Y. Tax Law" "601")) (round-cents (/ (* amount (int-to-float rate-pcm)) 100000.0)))

; The tax on taxable income from a rate schedule as printed: the base of the
; highest row whose floor the income exceeds, plus its rate on the excess.
(def ny-schedule-tax ((rows (Slice NyBand)) (taxable Money)) Money :cite ((law "N.Y. Tax Law" "601")) (withs (ti (clamp-zero taxable)) (fold (fn ((acc Money) (row NyBand)) Money (if (or (> ti (. row 'floor)) (is (. row 'floor) #usd"0.00")) (+ (. row 'base) (ny-rate-of (- ti (. row 'floor)) (. row 'rate_pcm))) acc)) #usd"0.00" rows)))

; New York's estimated tax: Tax Law § 685(c) and (d), with the rate under §
; 697(j), worked through on Form IT-2105.9, New York's own underpayment form.
; It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed newyorktaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/NY.json.gz holds.
;
; One computation covers four taxes: New York State personal income tax, the
; New York City resident tax, the Yonkers tax and the MCTMT on
; self-employment earnings. They are paid on one voucher, Form IT-2105, and
; the penalty for all of them is figured together on Form IT-2105.9, so this
; year's and last year's tax are the four combined, and New York's own facts
; say which apply.
;
; New York follows the federal rules: four 25% instalments, the lesser of 90%
; of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, 110% above $150,000 of last
; year's New York AGI, and payments applied to the earliest instalment first.
; It differs in the $300 threshold for each tax, the MCTD earnings step, and
; its own rate: the federal short-term rate plus 5½ points, not below 7½%,
; simple, set each quarter. The rate from January 1, 2027 is not published,
; so those days are not charged and the penalty says so.
;
; The figures follow IT-2105-I for 2026 and Form IT-2105.9 and its
; instructions for 2025, the latest published, with the 2026 dates; the
; answer's divergences say where the statute reads otherwise. Not built, as
; in the Go rules: the exception for an instalment due on or after the
; taxpayer's death (§ 685(d)(3)), the 90-day extension after a spouse's
; death, and estates and trusts. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the year's IT-2105-I and the department's
; interest rate pages print them.
(defstruct NewYorkEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (last_year_high_rate Int) (step Money) (step_separate Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (file_and_pay_by Date) (rates (Slice EstRate)))

(deffigures ny-estimated-2026 NewYorkEstimatedYear 2026 (from ny-dtf-it-2105-i-2026 (threshold #usd"300.00" :at who-must-pay) (this_year_rate 9000 :at penalty) (last_year_rate 10000 :at penalty) (last_year_high_rate 11000 :at penalty) (step #usd"150000.00" :at penalty) (step_separate #usd"75000.00" :at penalty) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at when-to-pay) (file_and_pay_by #date"2027-01-31" :at when-to-pay)) (from ny-dtf-interest-rates-2026 (rates (slice (EstRate #date"2026-04-01" #date"2026-06-15" 85000 "DTF, Interest rates: 4/1/2026–6/30/2026: § 697(j) underpayment rate 8.5%") (EstRate #date"2026-06-16" #date"2026-06-30" 85000 "DTF, Interest rates: 4/1/2026–6/30/2026: § 697(j) underpayment rate 8.5%") (EstRate #date"2026-07-01" #date"2026-09-15" 95000 "DTF, Interest rates: 7/1/2026–9/30/2026: § 697(j) underpayment rate 9.5%") (EstRate #date"2026-09-16" #date"2026-09-30" 95000 "DTF, Interest rates: 7/1/2026–9/30/2026: § 697(j) underpayment rate 9.5%") (EstRate #date"2026-10-01" #date"2026-12-31" 95000 "DTF, Interest rates: 10/1/2026–12/31/2026: § 697(j) underpayment rate 9.5%")) :at underpayment-rates)))

; How New York's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ny-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "New York expects estimated payments once tax after withholding is $300 or more. That is your state, New York City or Yonkers tax. It also expects them if you have any MCTMT. All four taxes go on one voucher, and the penalty is figured on them together." (slice "The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's total or 100% of last year's. You are clear if withholding and estimated payments for all four taxes reach it. A quarter is due by each of April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. As federally, last year's figure can become 110%. That happens if last year's New York AGI was over $150,000. The step is $75,000 if married filing separately. New York adds the same step for MCTD self-employment earnings. Last year's figure needs a full-year return." "There is no penalty if your tax due after withholding is under $300 a tax. That is $300 for each of the state, City and Yonkers taxes you pay. Nor is there one for a New York resident all last year with no New York tax due. Filing and paying in full by January 31 clears the January payment's penalty." "The penalty is simple interest on each shortfall for the days it stays unpaid. It stops on April 15 of the next year. Each payment goes first to the oldest shortfall. New York sets its own rate each quarter. It is the federal short-term rate plus 5½ points, never below 7½%. For 2026 that was 8.5% from April to June and 9.5% from July. The Department can waive the penalty for a casualty. It can also waive it for retiring after 62 or disability with reasonable cause.") "New York's threshold is $300 for each tax rather than $1,000. The City, Yonkers and MCTMT taxes are added in and figured together. MCTD self-employment earnings over $150,000 can trigger 110% on their own. New York uses its own rate, not the federal underpayment rate. It is the federal short-term rate plus 5½ points, with a 7½% floor." (slice "N.Y. Tax Law §§ 685(c), (d), 697(j); N.Y. Gen. Constr. Law § 25-a" "IT-2105-I (2026), Instructions for Form IT-2105, Estimated Tax Payment Voucher for Individuals" "IT-2105.9-I (2025), Instructions for Form IT-2105.9, Underpayment of Estimated Tax" "Department of Taxation and Finance, Interest rates for each quarter of 2026")))
