; Ohio's estimated income tax: Ohio Revised Code 5747.09, worked through on
; IT/SD 2210, Ohio's own underpayment form. It is written on the shared
; machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces
; the Go rules in the removed ohiotaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/OH.json.gz holds.
;
; Ohio's rules look like the federal ones in outline: 90% of this year's tax
; or 100% of last year's, in four quarters, with nothing due at $500 or less
; after withholding. They differ in how the penalty is figured. IT/SD 2210
; first tests the whole year: if withholding and timely payments reach the
; target, there is no penalty however they were spread. Otherwise it compares
; running totals at each due date and charges each shortfall at one factor
; for the span to the next due date, the last span ending April 15. A payment
; made between two due dates counts only from the next one. Last year's tax
; counts only after a timely return (line 6).
;
; The figures follow the 2026 IT 1040ES and the 2025 IT/SD 2210, the latest
; published, whose factors are worked out by the formula its page 4 gives,
; the rate times the days late over 365.25, to six places, each charge
; rounded to the dollar. The rate from January 1, 2027 is not published, so
; those days are not charged and the penalty says so. The answer's
; divergences say where ORC 5747.09 reads otherwise. Ohio's school district
; and city income taxes take their own estimated payments and are not
; covered. A year with no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the year's IT 1040ES prints them.
(defstruct OhioEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)))

; The 2026 figures.
(deffigures oh-estimated-2026 OhioEstimatedYear 2026 (from oh-dot-it-1040es-2026 (threshold #usd"500.00" :at who-must-pay) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at due-dates)))

; A tax year's rules: its figures, and what IT/SD 2210 gives it.
(defstruct OhioEstimatedRules (figures OhioEstimatedYear) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (shares (Slice Int)) (holidays (Slice Date)) (stop Date) (rates (Slice EstRate)) (day_count Int) (places Int) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How Ohio's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these rules
; carry.
(= oh-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Take this year's Ohio tax after credits, less Ohio withholding. If that is more than $500, Ohio expects estimated payments. The penalty is interest on what was short at each due date." (slice "There is no penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's Ohio tax or 100% of last year's. Last year's figure counts only if you filed last year's Ohio return on time. So if you filed no Ohio return last year, only the 90% figure is open to you. There is no 110% tier for higher incomes." "Pay a quarter each by April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates, whenever it was withheld. The department's form looks at the whole year first. Withholding and payments made by the January date may reach the target. If so, there is no penalty, even when the earlier quarters were short." "Otherwise the form compares each date's need with what had been paid by then. Each shortfall is charged interest from that date to the next one. The last is charged to April 15. A payment made between two dates counts only from the next date. The rate is set once for each calendar year, 7% for 2026. The form divides the year into 365.25 days." "Since tax year 2025 the law says the penalty may be added. The Tax Commissioner may reduce or remove it. Ohio's school district and city income taxes take their own estimated payments. Those are separate from these.") "Unlike federal, Ohio's threshold is more than $500 after withholding. The federal one is $1,000. There is no 110% tier. Last year's tax counts only after a timely Ohio return. Meeting the whole year's target means no penalty however payments were spread. The interest runs to April 15 at a yearly rate. There's no casualty or retirement waiver." (slice "Ohio Revised Code 5747.09, as amended by HB 96 (136th General Assembly); 5703.47; 1.14" "IT/SD 2210, Interest Penalty on Underpayment of Tax, and its instructions, 2025" "IT 1040ES, Ohio Estimated Income Tax Payment Worksheet and Instructions, 2026" "Ohio Tax Alert, Updates to Ohio Form IT/SD 2210 (tax year 2017)")))

; The 2026 rules. The 2026 IT/SD 2210 is not published, so its figures are
; the 2025 form's: the 90% and 100% tests, the columns, the April 15 end of
; the last span, 365.25 days and six places. The 7% rate for 2026 is printed
; on the 2025 form's page 4 and set under ORC 5703.47; the rate for 2027 is
; not published. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are
; written out rather than deffigures. The holidays are ORC 1.14's from
; January 2026 to April 2027; none moves a 2026 due date.

; Oklahoma's estimated tax: 68 O.S. §§ 2385.7, 2385.9 and 2385.13, worked
; through on Form OW-8-P, which follows federal Form 2210's shape. Oklahoma
; calls the charge interest. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed oklahomataxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/OK.json.gz holds.
;
; The shape is federal: the lesser of a share of this year's tax and 100% of
; last year's, four equal quarters, and interest by the day on each
; quarter's shortfall. The numbers are not. This year's share is 70%, there
; is no higher prior-year share at any income, payments are needed from $500
; of tax over withholding, and the interest is 20% a year, fixed by statute.
; Farmers are not required to make payments at all. The figures follow the
; Oklahoma Tax Commission's forms, OW-8-ES (revised 6-2025) for 2026 and
; OW-8-P for 2025, and the answer's divergences say where the statutes read
; otherwise. A year with no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as Form OW-8-ES for the year prints them.
(defstruct OklahomaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (small_tax Money) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (rates (Slice EstRate)))

; The 2026 figures. The rate is set by statute, not by notice, so every day
; to the April 15, 2027 stop has one.
(deffigures ok-estimated-2026 OklahomaEstimatedYear 2026 (from ok-otc-form-ow-8-es-2026 (threshold #usd"500.00" :at who-must-pay) (small_tax #usd"1000.00" :at interest) (this_year_rate 7000 :at who-must-pay) (last_year_rate 10000 :at who-must-pay) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at due-dates) (rates (slice (EstRate #date"2026-01-01" #date"2027-04-15" 200000 "68 O.S. § 2385.13(A): 20% a year, fixed by statute")) :at interest)))

(deffigures ok-estimated-annualised-2026 OklahomaEstimatedAnnualised 2026 (from ok-otc-form-ow-8-es-sup-2026 (period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :at columns) (annualised_shares (slice 1750 3500 5250 7000) :at applicable-percentage)))

(defstruct OklahomaEstimatedRules (figures OklahomaEstimatedYear) (annualised OklahomaEstimatedAnnualised) (shares (Slice Int)) (holidays (Slice Date)) (file_and_pay_by Date) (stop Date) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How Oklahoma's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ok-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Oklahoma expects estimated payments once tax tops withholding by $500 or more. Paying too little by a due date costs interest of 20% a year on the shortfall." (slice "You avoid interest if withholding plus estimated payments reach a target. It's the smaller of 70% of this year's tax or all the tax on last year's return. Last year's figure needs a twelve-month return and is the same at every income." "A quarter is due April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A date on a weekend or Tax Commission closure shifts to the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly across the four dates, whenever it was taken." "There is no interest if this year's tax after credits is under $1,000. There is none if it is less than $500 above your withholding. Nor is there any if you didn't have to file an Oklahoma return last year." "Oklahoma calls the charge interest. It is 20% a year, set by statute, and charged by the day from each due date. It runs until the shortfall is paid, or April 15 of the next year if sooner. A payment goes first to the oldest shortfall. For uneven income, the annualised method can lower early payments. Its form is OW-8-P-SUP-I. The statute also waives the January payment if you file and pay by January 31. The Tax Commission's forms don't apply that. There is no waiver for a casualty, retirement or disability.") "Unlike federal, payments start at $500 over withholding, not $1,000. This year's share is 70%, not 90%. Last year's share is 100% at every income, with no 110% tier. The interest is a fixed 20% a year. The annualised percentages are 17.5%, 35%, 52.5% and 70%. There's no casualty or disability waiver." (slice "68 O.S. §§ 2385.7, 2385.9, 2385.13" "Form OW-8-ES, Oklahoma Individual Estimated Tax, tax year 2026 (revised 6-2025)" "Form OW-8-P, Underpayment of Estimated Tax Worksheet, 2025" "Forms OW-8-ES-SUP (2026) and OW-8-P-SUP-I (2025), annualised income installment method" "2025 Oklahoma Resident Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form 511 packet), lines 22 and 40")))

; The 2026 rules. The 2026 OW-8-P is not published, so its 25% instalments
; are the 2025 form's; the January 31 date and the April 15 stop are the
; statute's, and the holidays are those 25 O.S. § 82.1(A) fixes from January
; 2026 to February 2027. The extra Christmas day for 2026 is chosen by the
; Governor's Executive Order, so it is left out; no due date is near it. A
; figure's source must be for its year, so these are written out rather than
; deffigures.

; Oregon's estimated tax: ORS 316.557 to 316.589, with interest at the rate
; set under ORS 305.220, worked through on Form OR-10. It is written on the
; shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and
; reproduces the Go rules in the removed oregontaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/OR.json.gz holds.
;
; Oregon's rules look like the federal ones and differ in the details that
; change a number. The prior-year test is 100% at every income. Farmers and
; fishers owe no estimates at all. Due dates move for Oregon's own legal
; holidays. A late starter pays in fewer, larger instalments, and a part-year
; resident divides the payment over the periods of residence. The charge is
; interest, which Form OR-10 figures on a running balance from one event to
; the next, at a printed daily factor, each line in whole dollars. The
; figures follow Publication OR-ESTIMATE for 2026 and the Form OR-10
; instructions for 2025, and the answer's divergences say where the statutes
; or rules read otherwise. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.

It needs a full 12-month return filed before this year's. If you had no Oregon return last year, only the 90% figure is available." "Pay a quarter by April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. You can instead pay the whole amount by April 15. A date on a weekend or an Oregon legal holiday shifts to the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly on those dates. You can instead show when it was withheld. If you first need to pay after April 1, you pay fewer, larger installments. They are three, two or one equal installments from the next date." "The interest runs on the unpaid balance from one event to the next. Each installment raises the balance, and withholding and payments lower it. Payments go to the oldest unpaid installment first. The rate is 8% for 2026, charged at a daily rate the department prints. Interest stops when the balance is paid or on April 15 of the next year. Uneven income can use the annualised method on Form OR-10. It uses 22.5%, 45%, 67.5% and 90% of the annualised tax." "There is no interest if your tax after credits less withholding is under $1,000. It can do the same for retiring at 62 or older or becoming disabled. That needs reasonable cause.") "Unlike federal, the prior-year test is 100% at every income, with no 110% tier. Due dates move for Oregon's own legal holidays. The charge is interest on a running balance, with each line in whole dollars. A late starter pays in fewer, larger installments." ; Pennsylvania's estimated tax: Tax Reform Code of 1971 §§ 325, 326 and

; golden/testdata/estimated/PA.json.gz holds.
;
; Pennsylvania differs from the federal rules in shape, not only in numbers.
; Whether payments are needed turns on income received without withholding.
; The prior-year test is last year's taxable income at this year's rate, not
; last year's tax. The penalty is measured against 90% of this year's tax in
; every case, and the prior-year test and the income-to-date test are
; exceptions that take the interest off an instalment rather than lowering
; it. A filer who first meets the requirement late can have the earlier
; instalments excused, but only under the special exception.
;
; The figures follow REV-413 (I) for 2026 and REV-1630 for 2025, the latest
; published, and the answer's divergences say where the Tax Reform Code reads
; otherwise. A year with no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.

; How Pennsylvania's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= pa-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Pennsylvania expects estimated payments for 2026 if two things are true. You have $14,000 or more of income with no Pennsylvania tax withheld. You also have $430 or more due after withholding and credits. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall." (slice "Withholding, credits and estimated payments must reach a target. That avoids the penalty. The target is the smaller of two figures. One is 90% of this year's tax. The other is last year's Pennsylvania taxable income at this year's 3.07% rate. Last year's Tax Forgiveness Credit comes off that one. Pennsylvania does not use last year's tax itself, and there is no 110% tier." "The payments are a quarter each. They're due April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. Withholding and credits count evenly across the four dates, whenever they came. A final return filed and paid by January 31 counts as the January payment." "The penalty is figured against 90% of this year's tax in every quarter. The prior-year figure does not lower that amount. It excuses a quarter outright if payments by its date reach that figure so far. So does paying 90% of the tax on income actually received by each period's end. That helps when income arrives late in the year. The interest is charged by the day, at a rate set once each calendar year. It stops on April 15 of the next year." "You may only learn partway through the year that you must pay. The department still expects a quarter for each date. It charges interest on the earlier ones until you catch up. If none were due from you the year before, it excuses the earlier quarters. You must pay the whole catch-up by the first date that applies to you. There's no penalty in the year after one with 100% Tax Forgiveness.") "Pennsylvania's rules start from income without withholding, not $1,000 of tax. The prior-year test is last year's income at this year's rate. There's no 110% tier. It and the income-to-date test excuse a quarter rather than lowering it. The income-to-date test uses actual income without annualising. The rate is set for each calendar year. There's no casualty, retirement or disability waiver." ; The Rhode Island Tax Computation Worksheet: taxable income times the rate
; for its band, less the band's subtraction amount.

Laws" "44-30-2.6")) (bind ti (clamp-zero taxable)) (bind c1 (. y 'bracket_1_ceiling)) (bind c2 (. y 'bracket_2_ceiling)) (bind r1 (int-to-float (. y 'rate_1_bp))) (bind r2 (int-to-float (. y 'rate_2_bp))) (bind r3 (int-to-float (. y 'rate_3_bp))) (line "a" "Taxable income from RI-1040 line 7" ti) (line "c" "Multiply (a) by the band's rate" (round-cents (cond ((<= linea c1) (/ (* linea r1) 10000.0)) ((<= linea c2) (/ (* linea r2) 10000.0)) (else (/ (* linea r3) 10000.0))))) (line "d" "The band's subtraction amount" (cond ((<= linea c1) #usd"0.00") ((<= linea c2) (round-cents (/ (* c1 (- r2 r1)) 10000.0))) (else (+ (round-cents (/ (* c1 (- r2 r1)) 10000.0)) (round-cents (/ (* c2 (- r3 r2)) 10000.0)))))) (line "e" "Subtract (d) from (c)" (clamp-zero (- linec lined))) (result linee))

; The tax on an amount through the 2025 rate schedule, unrounded: the band's
; rate on the whole amount, less the band's subtraction amount, as the Tax

; Rhode Island's estimated tax: R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 44-30-55, 44-30-56 and
; 44-30-84, worked through on Form RI-2210, which follows federal Form 2210's
; shape. It is written on the shared machinery in

;
; The shape is federal: the smaller of a share of this year's tax and all of
; last year's, four equal instalments, simple interest on each shortfall. The
; numbers are not: 80% rather than 90%, 100% of last year's tax at every
; income, a $250 floor, and a rate set once for each calendar year, 12% for
; 2026. Due dates move for Rhode Island's own legal holidays. The figures
; follow the Division of Taxation's forms, the 2026 RI-1040ES and the 2025
; RI-2210, the latest published, and the answer's divergences say where the
; General Laws read otherwise. A year with no figures is answered

; How Rhode Island's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ri-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Take your Rhode Island tax after credits and withholding. If it comes to $250 or more, Rhode Island expects estimated payments. The charge for paying too little is interest on each quarter's shortfall. It is 12% a year for 2026." (slice "There is no charge if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 80% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. Last year's figure stays at 100% however high your income was. There is also no charge if this year's tax less withholding is $250 or less. There is none either if you had no federal tax liability last year. You must also have lived in Rhode Island all that year." "Pay four equal quarters, by April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. The January date is in the next year. A weekend or Rhode Island legal holiday shifts a date to the next business day. None of the 2026 dates falls on one. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates. You can instead show when it was actually withheld. A payment goes first to the oldest shortfall." "The interest runs by the day from each due date until the shortfall is paid. It stops on April 15 of the next year. The rate is set once a year, at the prime rate plus 2%, but never below 12%. It was 12% for 2025 and is 12% for 2026. The annualised method on Form RI-2210 can lower early quarters. It helps when income arrives late in the year." "Filing your return early can stand in for the January payment. The penalty form counts a return filed and paid by January 31. The payment coupon says February 15. For 2026 the later date is February 16, 2027. February 15 is Washington's Birthday. The Division hasn't said which date it applies.") "Rhode Island uses 80% of this year's tax rather than 90%. It uses 100% of last year's at every income, with no 110% tier. Its floor is $250 rather than $1,000. Its rate is fixed for each calendar year rather than reset each quarter. Due dates move for Rhode Island's own holidays. The law adopts no waiver for a casualty, retirement or disability." (slice "R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 44-30-55, 44-30-56, 44-30-84, 44-30-91, 44-1-7 and 25-1-1" "280-RICR-20-55-1, Estimated Payments" "2026 RI-1040ES, Rhode Island Resident and Nonresident Estimated Payment Coupons" "2025 Form RI-2210 and its instructions, and 2025 Form RI-2210A" "ADV 2025-23, Interest rates posted for 2026 (November 26, 2025)")))

; The 2026 rules. The 2026 RI-2210 is not published, so its figures are the
; 2025 form's, with the 2026 dates: the quarters, the January 31 date, the
; April 15 stop and the annualised periods and percentages; the $2 minimum
; is the statute's. The holidays are § 25-1-1's from the first due date to
; February 16, 2027, the last date these rules move, less election day and
; days a governor or president appoints, which no checked-in document

;
; The return starts from the prepared federal return: federal taxable income,
; the federal filing status and the dependents the federal return claims.
; Additions are lettered a to e and subtractions f to w. Credits, the state
; tax addback and refund, and military retirement deductions are inputs.

; the form, instructions and tax tables they implement name them in
; sources/catalog/sc/2025.

; ceiling, the SC1040TT tables give the tax on the middle of the row the
; income falls in; at or above it, the rate schedule applies to the income
; itself. Either way the tax is in whole dollars.

"12-6-510")) (withs (ti (clamp-zero income) rate (fn ((x Money)) Money (cond ((<= x (. y 'zero_bracket_top)) #usd"0.00") ((<= x (. y 'low_bracket_top)) (/ (* (- x (. y 'zero_bracket_top)) (int-to-float (. y 'low_rate_bp))) 10000.0)) (else (- (/ (* x (int-to-float (. y 'top_rate_bp))) 10000.0) (. y 'top_rate_subtraction)))))) (if (>= ti (. y 'tax_table_ceiling)) (round-dollar (rate ti)) (withs (width (if (< ti (. y 'narrow_row_ceiling)) (. y 'narrow_row_width) (. y 'wide_row_width)) row-floor (* width (floor-float (/ ti width))) midpoint (+ row-floor (/ width 2.0))) (round-dollar (rate midpoint))))))

; golden/testdata/estimated/SC.json.gz holds.
;
; § 12-54-55(1) also charges no penalty on an underpayment caused by personal
; service income earned in another state that withheld its own tax, and
; § 12-6-3910(A) fixes the four due dates. The rate is set under
; § 12-54-25(D) in the same manner and at the same time as the federal
; underpayment rate. The figures follow the department's forms: the 2026
; SC1040ES and the 2025 SC2210, the latest penalty form. Where they part from
; each other or from the statute, the answer's divergences say so. A year

; How South Carolina's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years
; these rules carry.
(= sc-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "South Carolina uses the federal estimated tax rules, but its threshold is $100. The federal threshold is $1,000. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall." (slice "There is no penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. The second figure is 110% if last year's AGI was over $150,000. The AGI limit is $75,000 for married filing separately. Last year's figure needs a South Carolina return covering a full twelve months. There is no penalty if this year's tax less withholding is under $100. There is also none after a full twelve months with $0 of South Carolina tax." "Pay a quarter each by April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A weekend or South Carolina legal holiday moves a date to the next business day. The state list has days the federal one lacks, such as Confederate Memorial Day. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates. You can instead show when it was actually withheld. Filing and paying the balance by February 1, 2027 excuses the January payment. The earlier shortfalls then stop accruing on January 15." "The penalty is simple interest on a shortfall for the days it stays unpaid. The department's rate follows the federal underpayment rate. Each day is charged the rate divided by 365. Interest stops on April 15 of the next year. A payment goes first to the oldest shortfall. For 2026 the rate is 6% from April to June and 7% after. If income came unevenly, the federal Schedule AI can lower the early payments. You complete it for South Carolina." "The department can waive the penalty for a casualty or disaster. It can also do so for retirement after 62 or disability, with reasonable cause. The 2026 estimate worksheet predates the 2026 rate cut. Use the new rates for this year's tax before comparing it with these targets.") "South Carolina differs from federal in four ways that can change a number. Its threshold is $100 rather than $1,000. There is no penalty on an underpayment from income earned in another state. That state must have withheld its tax. South Carolina has its own legal holidays. A return can be filed and paid by the end of January. Then earlier shortfalls stop accruing on January 15." (slice "S.C. Code §§ 12-6-3910, 12-54-25 and 12-54-55; 26 U.S.C. § 6654" "SC1040ES, Individual Declaration of Estimated Tax, 2026 (Rev. 10/13/25)" "SC2210, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, Estates, and Trusts, 2025 (Rev. 12/02/25)" "SC Information Letter #26-19 (interest rate); SC Revenue Procedure #23-1 (legal holidays)" "Act No. 110 of 2026; SC Information Letter #26-20")))

; Utah's prepayment rules: Utah Code §§ 59-10-516 and 59-1-401(5), worked
; through on the Payment Worksheet of Form TC-546 with the extension penalty
; of Publication 58. They are written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduce the Go rules in
; the removed utahtaxcalc, whose answers golden/testdata/estimated/UT.json.gz
; holds.
;
; Utah has no estimated tax for individuals. Nothing is due during the year,
; and a return filed and paid by its due date owes no prepayment penalty
; however little was paid before. The one rule is the extension test: a
; filer who uses the automatic six-month extension must have paid, by the
; original due date, the lesser of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last
; year's. A filer who did not is charged 2% a month of the tax unpaid on that
; date, for the months of the extension. So the requirement is that one
; test, the schedule is that one date, and the penalty is the extension
; penalty. Interest and the late-payment penalty on a balance paid after the
; due date are a different charge and are not figured here.
;
; The figures follow TC-546 (Rev. 10/26) for the test and Publication 58
; (Rev. 11/25) for the arithmetic; the answer's divergences say where the
; Utah Code reads otherwise. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as TC-546 and Publication 58 print them.
(defstruct UtahEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (penalty_rate Int) (penalty_cap Int))

; The 2026 figures.
(deffigures ut-estimated-2026 UtahEstimatedYear 2026 (from ut-usc-form-tc-546-2026 (this_year_rate 9000 :at payment-worksheet) (last_year_rate 10000 :at payment-worksheet)) (from ut-usc-pub-58-2026 (penalty_rate 2400 :at extension-penalty) (penalty_cap 1200 :at extension-penalty)))

; A tax year's rules: its figures and its dates.
(defstruct UtahEstimatedRules (figures UtahEstimatedYear) (due Date) (extension_ends Date) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How Utah's prepayment rules work, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ut-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Utah has no estimated tax, and nothing is due during the year. The only prepayment rule is for a return filed late on an extension. Utah's extension is automatic and lasts six months." (slice "A 2026 Utah return filed and paid by April 15, 2027 has no prepayment penalty. That holds however little was withheld or paid during the year. You can still prepay at any time if you want to." "Utah gives six more months to file without asking, to October 15, 2027. But by April 15 your withholding and prepayments must reach a minimum. It is the lesser of 90% of your 2026 Utah tax or 100% of your 2025 Utah tax. Withholding counts in full whenever it was taken. If you filed for 2025 with no tax due, the minimum is nothing. If you didn't file at all, the Tax Commission asks for 90% of this year's tax." "Miss the minimum and the penalty is steep. It is 2% a month of all the tax still unpaid on April 15. It is worked out by the day until you file, for up to six months, or 12%. It is charged on the whole unpaid balance, not just the shortfall. The late-payment penalty and interest on unpaid tax are added from April 15. If you do not file by October 15, the extension is lost. The late-filing and late-payment penalties then apply instead. The Tax Commission can waive a penalty for reasonable cause.") "Utah differs from federal in kind. There are no quarterly payments and no quarterly penalty. A return filed by April 15 has no prepayment penalty at all. The one test is on April 15, for an extended return. It has no 110% tier for high income. The penalty is 2% a month of everything unpaid, not interest on each shortfall. So a small shortfall can bring a large penalty." (slice "Utah Code §§ 59-10-514, 59-10-516, 59-1-401" "TC-40, Utah Individual Income Tax Instructions, 2025" "TC-546, Individual Income Tax Prepayment Coupon (Rev. 10/26)" "Publication 58, Utah Interest and Penalties (Rev. 11/25)")))

; Virginia's estimated tax: Code of Virginia §§ 58.1-490 to 58.1-492 and
; § 58.1-15, worked through on Form 760C, Virginia's own underpayment form.

; Virginia follows the federal outline with different dates and a different
; order. The four instalments are due May 1, June 15, September 15 and
; January 15. Each is measured against the lesser of 90% of this year's tax
; and 100% of last year's. A payment made on an instalment date pays that
; instalment before any earlier shortfall. Four exceptions cancel the
; addition to tax for an instalment without lowering its shortfall, and
; there is no addition when the year's shortfalls total $1,000 or less. The
; addition is interest at the federal underpayment rate plus 2%.

; published, and the answer's divergences say where the Code reads
; otherwise. 2026 Acts c. 7 raised the small-underpayment exception from the
; 2025 form's $150 to $1,000, and the law's $1,000 is used. A year with no

; Form IN-111, Vermont Income Tax Return, for full-year residents.
;
; The return starts from the prepared federal return: federal AGI, the
; federal filing status and the dependents the federal return claims.
; Vermont's modifications, credits and refundable credits come in as inputs:
; Schedules IN-112, IN-117 and IN-119 are not worked here, nor is the
; property tax credit or renter credit.
;
; The rules cite the law (32 V.S.A. chapter 151). The parts of the form and
; instructions they implement name them in sources/catalog/vt/2025.
; The tax on taxable income through a rate schedule: the row's base plus its
; rate on the amount over the row's floor, rounded to the dollar.
(def vt-schedule-tax ((rows (Slice VermontScheduleRow)) (taxable Money)) Money :cite ((law "32 V.S.A." "5822")) (withs (ti (clamp-zero taxable) row (fold (fn ((acc VermontScheduleRow) (r VermontScheduleRow)) VermontScheduleRow (if (> ti (. r 'over)) r acc)) (VermontScheduleRow #usd"0.00" #usd"0.00" 0) rows)) (round-dollar (+ (. row 'base) (/ (* (- ti (. row 'over)) (int-to-float (. row 'rate_bp))) 10000.0)))))

; The rate, in basis points, on the next dollar of taxable income.
(def vt-marginal-rate-bp ((rows (Slice VermontScheduleRow)) (taxable Money)) Int :cite ((law "32 V.S.A." "5822")) (fold (fn ((acc Int) (r VermontScheduleRow)) Int (if (or (> taxable (. r 'over)) (is (. r 'over) #usd"0.00")) (. r 'rate_bp) acc)) 0 rows))

; The tax from the tax tables, for taxable income under $75,000: the rate
; schedule applied to the middle of the $100 row the income falls in. The
; first row, under $100, is taxed nothing.
(def vt-table-tax ((rows (Slice VermontScheduleRow)) (taxable Money)) Money :cite ((law "32 V.S.A." "5822")) (withs (ti (clamp-zero taxable)) (if (< ti #usd"100.00") #usd"0.00" (withs (steps (floor-float (/ ti #usd"100.00")) midpoint (+ (* #usd"100.00" steps) #usd"50.00")) (vt-schedule-tax rows midpoint)))))

; Form IN-111 line 8: the tax from the table or rate schedule, and at least
; 3% of federal AGI when that is over $150,000.
(def vt-income-tax ((y VermontYear) (rows (Slice VermontScheduleRow)) (fed-agi Money) (taxable Money)) Money :cite ((law "32 V.S.A." "5822")) (if (> fed-agi (. y 'minimum_tax_agi_threshold)) (max (vt-schedule-tax rows taxable) (round-dollar (/ (* fed-agi (int-to-float (. y 'minimum_tax_rate_bp))) 10000.0))) (if (< taxable (. y 'tax_table_limit)) (vt-table-tax rows taxable) (vt-schedule-tax rows taxable))))

; Vermont's estimated tax: 32 V.S.A. §§ 5851, 5852 and 5859, with interest at
; the rate the Commissioner sets under § 3108 and the penalty of § 3202(b)(2),
; worked through on Worksheet IN-152, or IN-152A for a filer who annualises.
; It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed vermonttaxcalc, whose answers golden/testdata/estimated/VT.json.gz
; holds.
;
; The required annual payment is the lesser of 90% of this year's tax and
; 100% of last year's, from a full-year return, a quarter on each due date.
; Withholding always counts as paid a quarter on each due date. A shortfall is
; charged twice: interest by the day at each calendar year's rate, and a
; penalty of 1% for each month or part of a month, each on the quarter's whole
; underpayment until it is paid in full. Nothing is charged when this year's
; tax less withholding is under $500, and a filer with two-thirds of gross
; income from farming or fishing, this year or last, owes no estimates.
;
; A filer who annualises federally may annualise Vermont's too: Worksheet
; IN-152A scales each federal Schedule AI installment by the Vermont required
; annual payment over the federal one. Those figures come from the federal
; answer to the same request, read only when the request gives federal
; figures.
;
; The figures follow the 2026 IN-114 instructions and the 2025 worksheets,
; the latest published, with the 2026 dates; the answer's divergences say where
; the worksheets and the statute part ways. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the IN-114 instructions for the year print them.
(defstruct VermontEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (threshold Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)))

; The 2026 figures.
(deffigures vt-estimated-2026 VermontEstimatedYear 2026 (from vt-tax-form-in-114-instructions-2026 (this_year_rate 9000 :at liability) (last_year_rate 10000 :at liability) (threshold #usd"500.00" :at liability) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at due-dates)))

; How Vermont's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these rules
; carry.
(= vt-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Vermont expects estimated payments when withholding will not cover your tax. If you fall short, it charges interest on each quarter's shortfall. It also charges a separate penalty of 1% a month. Neither applies if this year's tax less withholding is under $500." (slice "You are clear if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. Last year's figure counts only if you filed a full-year return. There is no 110% tier for high incomes." "The payments are a quarter each. They're due April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. Withholding counts as paid evenly across the four dates, whenever it was taken. If you annualise your federal estimates, you can annualise Vermont's too. They follow the federal installments in proportion." "Each quarter's shortfall is charged two ways. Both run until it is paid in full or until April 15 of the next year. Interest runs by the day at a rate set once each calendar year, 7.75% for 2026. The penalty is 1% of the shortfall for each month or part of a month. So a payment one day late costs a full 1%." "The Child Care Contribution applies to self-employed people working in Vermont. They should include it in their payments.") "Vermont differs from federal in six ways that change a number. Its threshold is $500, not $1,000. There's no 110% tier. A 1% monthly penalty comes on top of the interest. The whole shortfall is charged until it is paid in full. Withholding is always spread evenly. There's no casualty, retirement or disability waiver." (slice "32 V.S.A. §§ 3108, 3202(b)(2), 5851, 5852, 5859" "IN-114, Vermont Individual Income Estimated Tax Payment Voucher, and its instructions, 2026" "IN-152 and IN-152A, Underpayment of Estimated Individual Income Tax, 2025" "Vermont Department of Taxes, 2026 Interest Rate memo, November 4, 2025")))

; The 2026 rules. The 2026 IN-152 is not published, so its figures are the 2025
; worksheet's with the 2026 dates: the quarters, the April 15 stop, the 365-day
; year and the 1% a month. The 7.75% for 2026 is the rate the 2025 IN-152
; prints on line 9b, set by the Department's memo of November 4, 2025; the
; rate for 2027 is set by December 15, 2026 and is not published, so interest
; stops at the end of 2026. The holidays are the State Holiday Closures page's
; 2026 and 2027 columns, less its two 2026 Thanksgiving rows, which name a
; Saturday and a Sunday. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are

(= vt-estimated-rules-2026 VermontEstimatedRules (make-struct VermontEstimatedRules :figures vt-estimated-2026 :shares (slice 2500 2500 2500 2500) :holidays (slice #date"2026-01-01" #date"2026-01-19" #date"2026-02-16" #date"2026-03-03" #date"2026-05-25" #date"2026-07-03" #date"2026-09-07" #date"2026-10-12" #date"2026-11-11" #date"2026-12-25" #date"2027-01-01" #date"2027-01-18" #date"2027-02-15" #date"2027-03-02" #date"2027-05-31" #date"2027-06-18" #date"2027-07-05" #date"2027-09-06" #date"2027-10-11" #date"2027-11-11" #date"2027-11-25" #date"2027-11-26" #date"2027-12-24") :stop #date"2027-04-15" :rates (slice (EstRate #date"2026-01-01" #date"2026-12-31" 77500 "Vermont Department of Taxes, 2026 Interest Rate memo, November 4, 2025: 7.75% for 2026 under 32 V.S.A. § 3108")) :day_basis 365 :monthly 100 :explanation vt-estimated-explanation))

(= vt-estimated-years (Table Int VermontEstimatedRules) (table 2026 vt-estimated-rules-2026))

; The credits applied to the installments as IN-152 lines 5a to 7 apply them,
; with 32 V.S.A. § 5859(b)(2) where the worksheet is silent. A credit counts
; toward the first installment due on or after its date (line 5b). Credits on
; a due date go to that installment first, and what is left pays any earlier
; underpayment, oldest first (§ 5859(b)(2)(B)). A credit between due dates

; The Washington capital gains excise tax return, chapter 82.87 RCW.
;
; Washington taxes no wages and no personal income. What an individual may owe
; it is this excise tax on the sale or exchange of long-term capital assets:
; 7% of Washington capital gains above the standard deduction, and from 2025 a
; further 2.9% on the part above $1,000,000.
;
; The return is filed electronically and prints no line numbers, so the
; schema's fields are named for the statute's concepts and each step below
; cites the subsection it comes from.
;
; The gain starts from the federal return: Schedule D's net long-term capital
; gain (RCW 82.87.020). Gain the federal return carries on Schedule D line 11,
; from Form 4797 and the like, is from real estate and depreciable business
; property, which RCW 82.87.050 exempts, so it is taken out. So is any other
; exempt or out-of-state gain the filer reports. Allocation of gain on
; intangibles turns on where the filer was domiciled at the sale (RCW
; 82.87.100), which is a fact these rules take as given for a resident.

; 82.87.120(1)), separate for married filing separately, and individual

; Washington's capital gains tax payment: RCW 82.87.110 and 82.87.115, with
; the late payment penalty of RCW 82.32.090 and the interest of RCW
; 82.32.050. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; the removed washingtontaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/WA.json.gz holds.
;
; Washington has no quarterly estimated tax. The whole capital gains tax is
; due in one payment on the federal return's due date, and a filing extension
; doesn't move it. So there is one installment, no prior-year safe harbor, no
; withholding and no annualised method. The charge is not interest on a
; shortfall: it is a late payment penalty of 9%, 19% or 29% by lateness, or,
; for a filer with an extension who paid an estimate on time, 5% of the whole
; tax when the estimate was under 80% of it. Interest runs separately from the
; end of April.
;
; Washington prints no form for the payment; the answer's worksheet is
; CapitalGainsPayment, the computation step by step. The figures follow the
; Department of Revenue where its guidance is current, and the statute where
; the guidance predates SSB 5314 (chapter 409, Laws of 2025); the divergences
; say where the two part ways. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the department publishes them.
(defstruct WashingtonEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (due Date) (prepay_from Date) (rates (Slice EstRate)))

; these rules carry.

It rises to 19% if still unpaid at the end of May, and 29% at the end of June. The penalty is at least $5. Separately, interest runs on unpaid tax from April 30, 2027. ; Go rules in the removed wisconsintaxcalc, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/WI.json.gz holds. Wisconsin calls the charge
; underpayment interest.
;
; The required annual payment is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax and
; 100% of last year's, with no 110% tier, in four equal installments, and
; nothing is charged when this year's tax less withholding is under $500.

; payments in: a payment counts first toward the installment of the period it
; was made in; only what is left goes back to an earlier shortfall, the most
; recent first, and then forward; a payment after January 15 goes to the
; January shortfall first. Form 2210 pays the oldest shortfall first.

; and its instructions, the latest published, with the 2026 dates; the
; answer's divergences say where Chapter 71 reads otherwise. A year with no
; figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.

; How West Virginia's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years
; these rules carry.
(= wv-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "West Virginia expects estimated payments if withholding leaves $600 or more due. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall, at 11.5% a year for 2026." (slice "You avoid the penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. A quarter of it is due by each date. Last year's figure counts only if that return covered a full 12 months. There is no 110% tier for higher incomes. A zero tax last year counts only while this year's tax is $5,000 or less. Then the penalty form asks for nothing. Above that, you need 90% of this year's tax." "The due dates are April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A date on a weekend or a legal holiday becomes the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly across the four dates. You can instead show when it was actually withheld. Filing and paying in full by the end of January excuses the January payment. For 2026 that means by Monday, February 1, 2027." "The penalty is charged daily on each date's shortfall. It runs until the shortfall is paid or April 15 of the next year. A payment goes first to the oldest shortfall. The rate is set once a year at the prime rate plus three points. The form prints it as a daily factor, 0.000315 for 2026. Form IT-210's annualized method can lower early quarters for uneven income. The Tax Division can waive the penalty for a casualty or for reasonable cause.") "West Virginia differs from federal in ways that change a number. Its threshold is $600, not the federal $1,000. It has no 110% prior-year tier. A zero tax last year counts only while this year's tax is $5,000 or less. The rate is set once a year, 11.5% for 2026, not each quarter. There's no waiver for retirement or disability." (slice "W.
